text: EX-10.4 6 ex10-4.htm EX-10.4 Exhibit 10.4 EXECUTION VERSION SIDE LETTER AGREEMENT November 2, 2026 Our Bond, Inc. 85 Broad Street New York, New York 10004 Attention: Doron Kempel, Chief Executive Officer Ascent Partners Fund LLC 19505 Biscayne Boulevard, Suite 2350 Aventura, Florida 33180 Attention: Mikhail Gurevich Re: Series G Exchange Transactions Ladies and Gentlemen: This letter agreement (this “Letter Agreement”) is entered into by Our Bond, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “Company”), and Ascent Partners Fund LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Ascent” or the “Holder”). Reference is made to (i) the exchange agreement dated November 2, 2026 between the Company and Ascent (the “Ascent Exchange Agreement”), (ii) the Amended and Restated Certificate of Designations, Preferences and Rights (the “Series G Certificate”) of the series G convertible preferred stock of the Company, par value $0.01 per share (the “Series G Preferred Stock”), to be filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Nevada and become effective at Closing (as defined below) (the “Series G Certificate”), (iii) the agreement dated as of the date hereof by and among the Company, Ascent and the applicable Eastward Fund Management, LLC (“Eastward”) holder or holders concerning Eastward’s purchase right, interest forgiveness and related exchange arrangements (the “Eastward Agreement”), (iv) the leak-out agreement, dated as of the date hereof, by and among the Company and Ascent (the “Leak-Out Agreement”), and (v) that certain amendment to the existing securities purchase agreement, dated as of October 27, 2025, as amended to date (such agreement the “ELOC”), by and among the Company and Ascent (the “ELOC Amendment”). For this Letter Agreement, “Transaction Documents” means this Letter Agreement, the Ascent Exchange Agreement, the Series G Certificate, the Eastward Agreement, the Leak-Out Agreement and the ELOC Amendment. The “Closing” shall mean the release of all signatures by all parties to the Transaction Documents. Capitalized terms not defined herein have the meanings in the Ascent Exchange Agreement or Series G Certificate, as applicable. In consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein and in the Transaction Documents, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the parties agree as follows: 1. Retirement of Existing Warrants. At the Closing, each warrant to purchase capital stock of the Company held by Ascent (the “Existing Warrants”) shall be surrendered and cancelled without further payment (the “Warrant Cancellation”). Ascent represents that it is the current holder of record of the Existing Warrants and holds such Existing Warrants free of any liens. The Company shall promptly update its records and notify its transfer agent and any warrant agent of the Warrant Cancellation. The Company represents and warrants to Ascent that it shall cancel all other warrants to purchase capital stock of the Company held by other holders in accordance with and pursuant to the terms of such other warrants. 2. Demand Registration Rights. (a) At any time after the date of this Letter Agreement, Ascent may demand the Company register the all shares of Common Stock issued or issuable upon conversion of its Series G Preferred Stock (the “Ascent Registrable Securities”) on Form S-1 or, when available, Form S-3, that are not covered at the time of such demand by an effective registration statement or if such shares may not otherwise at such time be sold under Rule 144 without volume or manner-of-sale limitations or a current-public-information requirement. This Letter Agreement constitutes a continuing demand effective at Closing. Ascent may identify additional Ascent Registrable Securities in a written demand notice (each such notice, a “Demand Notice”). Registration is not conditioned on exercise, expiration or settlement of any purchase right. (b) The Company shall file a resale registration statement covering the Ascent Registrable Securities within ten (10) calendar days after Closing, on Form S-3 if then available and otherwise on Form S-1. When Form S-3 first becomes available, the Company shall within ten (10) calendar days file a Form S-3 or an appropriate amendment to use that form for the then-outstanding Ascent Registrable Securities, regardless of whether the Company has filed a Form S-1 to register such securities. For additional Ascent Registrable Securities identified in a later Demand Notice, the Company shall file the required registration statement or amendment to a registration statement within ten (10) calendar days after receipt of such Demand Notice, using Form S-3 if available and otherwise Form S-1. The Company shall maintain existing effective coverage until replacement coverage is effective and available, without a registration gap. (c) The Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause each registration statement to become effective as promptly as practicable and keep it effective and available for resale until the earlier of (i) the date all Ascent Registrable Securities covered thereby have been sold and (ii) the date all such Ascent Registrable Securities may be sold pursuant to Rule 144 without volume or manner-of-sale limitations or a current-public-information requirement. The Company shall bear all customary registration expenses, other than selling commissions and fees and expenses of counsel separately engaged by Ascent, and shall provide Ascent customary review, notice, indemnification and cooperation rights. 3. S-1 Advances. (a) Advances. Following the filing by the Company of a registration statement on Form S-1 covering shares of Common Stock held by or issuable to Ascent (each, an “Applicable Registration Statement”), Ascent shall advance to the Company an aggregate principal amount of up to forty percent (40%) of the Registration Statement Value (each, an “Advance”). “Registration Statement Value” means the product of (i) the number of shares of Common Stock registered for resale on behalf of Ascent pursuant to the Applicable Registration Statement and (ii) the lowest VWAP during the ten (10) Trading Days immediately preceding the filing date of the Applicable Registration Statement. (b) Note. Each Advance shall be evidenced by a non-convertible promissory note in a form mutually agreed by the Company and Ascent (each, a “Note”). Each Note shall bear simple interest on its outstanding principal balance at a rate of ten percent (10%) per annum. (c) Good Faith. The Company shall act in good faith in preparing, filing and pursuing effectiveness of each Applicable Registration Statement and shall not take any action principally designed to increase the amount of an Advance or prevent, delay or avoid repayment of a Note. (d) Repayment from Next Capital Raise. Until each Note has been paid in full, the Company shall apply sixty percent (60%) of the cash proceeds received from the next issuance or sale of equity, equity-linked securities or indebtedness following the applicable Advance to the repayment of such Note. Any payment under this Section shall be applied first to accrued and unpaid interest and then to outstanding principal. 4. Mutual Release of Accrued Amounts. (a) Effective only at Closing and upon the simultaneous effectiveness of Eastward’s interest forgiveness under the Eastward Agreement, Ascent irrevocably waives all accrued and unpaid dividends through the Closing Date on the Series C preferred stock of the Company (“Series C Preferred Stock”), Series D preferred stock of the Company (“Series D Preferred Stock”), and existing Series G Preferred Stock held by Ascent on Schedule A (the “Released Dividends”). The Released Dividends total $555,203.33 as of October 29, 2026, comprising of (i) $110,323.52 of unpaid dividends owed to Ascent pursuant to the Series C Preferred Stock, (ii) $353,538.90 of unpaid dividends owed to Ascent pursuant to the Series D Preferred Stock, and $91,340.91 of unpaid dividends owed to Ascent pursuant to the Series G Preferred Stock, subject to reconciliation of accruals and payments through Closing. No Released Dividends shall be capitalized into the new Series G Preferred Stock to be issued in connection with the Ascent Exchange Agreement or any other exchange agreement to be executed in tandem with the Ascent Exchange Agreement, and no Released Dividends will remain payable on the Series G Preferred Stock outstanding prior to the execution of the Transaction Document after Closing. The principal balance on the Series G Preferred Stock outstanding prior to the execution of the Transaction Documents shall remain outstanding after Closing, and, after the Closing, dividends shall accrue on all Series G Preferred Stock pursuant to the terms of the Series G Certificate. (b) Ascent’s waiver set forth in section 3(a) above is conditioned upon the simultaneous waiver by Eastward of accrued and unpaid interest through Closing owed to Eastward pursuant to the terms of the Eastward Agreement in connection with the execution of the Transaction Documents at Closing. The Company shall deliver the executed Eastward Agreement and evidence of the concurrent effectiveness of the waiver set forth therein. (c) Ascent’s waiver is limited to the Released Dividends. Ascent does not release principal, post-Closing dividends or any other claim or right. (d) Effective only at Closing and to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, in further consideration for the execution of the waiver in this Letter Agreement by the Holder and without limiting any rights or remedies the Holder may have, the Company, for itself and for its Subsidiaries, and each Subsidiary executing a the joinder hereto, each for itself, hereby releases each of the Holder and each of its Related Parties (each a “Releasee” and, collectively, the “Releasees”) from any and all Claims that any of the Company or its Subsidiaries has or may have against any Releasee, whether or not relating to any Transaction Document, any obligation or liability owing thereunder, any asset of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries or Affiliates, or any legal relationship that exists or may exist between any Releasee and any of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries. The Company, for itself and for its Subsidiaries, acknowledges and agrees that it or its Subsidiaries may discover information later that could have affected materially its willingness to agree to the release in this paragraph and that neither such possibility, which it took into account when executing this Letter Agreement, nor such discovery, as to which it expressly assumes the risk, shall affect the effectiveness of the release in this paragraph, and waives the benefit of any legal requirement that may provide otherwise. As used in this paragraph, (i) “Claims” means all liabilities, rights, demands, covenants, duties, obligations (including, without limitation, indebtedness, receivables and other contractual obligations), claims, actions and causes of actions, suits, disputes, judgments, damages, settlements, losses, debts, responsibilities, fines, penalties, sanctions, commissions and interest, disbursements, taxes, charges, interest, costs, fees and expenses (including, without limitation, fees, charges and disbursements of financial, legal and other advisors, consultants and professionals and, if applicable, any value-added and other taxes and charges thereon), in each case of any kind or nature, whether joint or several, whether now existing or hereafter arising and however acquired and whether or not known, asserted, direct, contingent, liquidated, due, consequential, actual, punitive or treble and (ii) “Related Party” means, with respect to any Person, any Affiliate of such Person or of another Related Party of such Person and such Person’s and such Affiliate’s predecessors, successors, assigns, managers, members, partners, directors, officers, staff members (including, without limitation, individuals with independent contractor or similar status), agents, attorneys-in-fact, trustees, fiduciaries, representatives and advisors. (e) Each Releasee may enforce Section 4(d) as an express third-party beneficiary. Each Subsidiary releasing claims shall execute the attached joinder before Closing. 4. Escrow Closing and Disclosure. (a) By 6:00 a.m., New York time, on Monday, November 2, 2026 (the “Disclosure Deadline”), the Company shall file on EDGAR a Current Report on Form 8-K disclosing all material terms of the transactions described in this Letter Agreement, with all material exhibits, and all other material nonpublic information concerning the Company or its Subsidiaries provided by or on behalf of the Company to Ascent or its representatives. Any accompanying press release shall be issued by the same deadline. The Company shall provide the public filing link and a certificate signed by its chief executive officer or chief financial officer confirming that no such information remains undisclosed (the “Disclosure Condition”). Ascent and its legal counsel shall receive the proposed filing of the Form 8-K including all material exhibits for reasonable review and comment. (b) This Letter Agreement shall become effective upon the Closing and only if, concurrently with the Closing: (a) each Exchange Agreement has become effective and the exchanges contemplated thereby have been consummated; (b) the Series G Certificate has been duly filed and become effective; (c) all Existing Warrants have been surrendered and cancelled; (d) the releases and waivers in Section 3 have become effective simultaneously; and (e) the Company has delivered evidence reasonably satisfactory to the Ascent of the foregoing actions. (c) Within one (1) Business Day after Closing, the Company shall obtain and deliver to Ascent a new reserve and instruction letter prepared by its transfer agent on its standard form, duly executed by the required parties. It shall reflect the current Series G Preferred Stock and reserves of Common Stock pursuant to the ELOC and the release or reallocation of shares of Common Stock underlying the cancelled Series C Preferred Stock, Series D Preferred Stock and warrant reserves. This deliverable does not postpone existing reserve, issuance or delivery obligations. (f) The escrow, disclosure and termination provisions bind upon signing. They control inconsistent provisions of the Transaction Documents as applicable to Ascent’s exchange and this Letter Agreement. After the Disclosure Condition is satisfied, the Company shall not provide Ascent or its representatives additional material nonpublic information without prior written consent and agreed disclosure arrangements. Actual disclosure and applicable law govern trading; a contractual confidentiality release is not a substitute. 5. Representations and Authority. Each party represents to the other parties that it has full power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Letter Agreement, the execution and delivery of this Letter Agreement and the performance of its obligations hereunder have been duly authorized, and this Letter Agreement constitutes its valid and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency and similar laws affecting creditors’ rights generally and general principles of equity. 6. Conflict; No Other Modification. In the event of a conflict between this Letter Agreement and any other Transaction Document with respect to the subject matter hereof, this Letter Agreement shall control as among the parties hereto. Except as expressly set forth herein, this Letter Agreement does not amend, modify or waive any provision of any Transaction Document, each of which remains in full force and effect. 7. Successors and Assigns. This Letter Agreement binds the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Neither party may assign it without the other’s written consent, except that Ascent may assign registration rights to a permitted transferee of the Ascent Registrable Securities upon written notice and that transferee’s written agreement to be bound by the applicable provisions. 8. Amendments; Waivers. Amendments and waivers require a writing signed by the Company and Ascent. No waiver of a breach waives any other or subsequent breach. 9. Notices. All notices under this Letter Agreement shall be in writing and delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of the applicable Exchange Agreement, with copies to the other parties at the addresses above or such other address as designated by written notice. 10. Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Jury Trial. This Letter Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the City of New York, Borough of Manhattan, in any action arising out of or relating to this Letter Agreement and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. EACH PARTY KNOWINGLY AND IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS LETTER AGREEMENT. 11. Entire Agreement; Counterparts; Electronic Signatures. This Letter Agreement and the Transaction Documents constitute the entire agreement among the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersede all prior discussions and understandings relating thereto. This Letter Agreement may be executed in counterparts. Electronic signatures, including signatures delivered through DocuSign or in PDF format, shall be effective as originals. text: EX-10.5 7 ex10-5.htm EX-10.5 Exhibit 10.5 LEAK-OUT AGREEMENT THIS LEAK-OUT AGREEMENT (the “ Agreement ”) is made and entered into as of November 2, 2026 by and among the undersigned holders (the “ Holders ”) and Our Bond, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “ Company ”). The Company and the Holders are each a “ Party ” and collectively are the “ Parties ”. Any capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall have their respective meanings ascribed to them in the Certificate of Designation (as defined below). RECITALS WHEREAS, the Holders beneficially own and hold a number of shares of the Company’s Series G Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the “ Series G Preferred Stock ”) set forth across from such Holder’s name in column (1) of Schedule A attached hereto (the “ Preferred Shares ”), which Series G Preferred Stock are convertible into shares of the Company’s common stock (the “ Conversion Shares”), par value $0.0001 per share (the “ Common Stock ”), pursuant to the terms set forth in the Certificate of Designations, Preferences and rights of the Series G Convertible Preferred Stock as in effect on the date hereof (the “ Certificate of Designation ”); and WHEREAS, the Company and the Holders desire to limit the number of shares of Common Stock each Holder is permitted to sell during the applicable time periods set forth herein. NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the foregoing premises and the mutual covenants contained herein, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1. Representations and Warranties . Each of the Parties hereto, by their respective execution and delivery of this Agreement, hereby represents and warrants to the others and to all third party beneficiaries of this Agreement that: (a) such Party has the full right, capacity and authority to enter into, deliver and perform its respective obligations under this Agreement, (b) this Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by such Party and is the binding and enforceable obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, and (c) the execution, delivery and performance of such Party’s obligations under this Agreement will not conflict with or breach the terms of any other agreement, contract, commitment or understanding to which such Party is a party or to which the assets or securities of such Party are bound. 2. Leak Out . (a) Except as otherwise expressly provided herein, and subject to any other restrictions prohibiting the conversion, offer, sale or transfer of shares of Common Stock under applicable United States federal or state securities laws, rules and regulations (collectively, the “ Regulations ”), the Company and the Holders agree that commencing, as to each Holder, only upon consummation of that Holder’s exchange under its separate exchange agreement (each, an “ Exchange Agreement ”) by and between the Company and such Holder (the “ Effective Time ”), subject to any applicable Regulations, each Holder shall be entitled to sell any shares of Common Stock held or acquired by such Holder, including Conversion Shares, in accordance with the restrictions contained under Section 2(b) hereunder (the “ Leak Out ”). In the event the Company terminates, reduces, waives or otherwise modifies any of the restrictions set forth in this Agreement with respect to any Holder, other than the information set forth on Schedule A different percentages and the express AP ELOC exception agreed herein, then the other Holders under this Agreement shall be entitled to the same modification of its restrictions hereunder. (b) Commencing at the Effective Time, subject to applicable Regulations, each Holder agrees, on behalf of itself and its affiliates that control, are controlled by or are under common investment discretion with such Holder with respect to shares of Common Stock (collectively, the “ Trading Affiliates ”), that while such Holder or any such Trading Affiliate holds any Preferred Shares, the aggregate number of shares of Common Stock sold or otherwise disposed of by such Holder and its Trading Affiliates on a Trading Day, measured immediately after each sale or disposition, shall not exceed: (i) Prior to the effective date of a registration statement registering the resale of Conversion Shares by Eastward Fund Management LLC , Maxim Group, LLC, and /or their respective Trading Affiliates, the applicable percentage in column (3) of Schedule A (the “ Leak-Out Percentage ”) of the cumulative reported trading volume of the Common Stock from the commencement of that Trading Day’s pre-market session through the time of such sale or disposition. On any Trading Day on which: (w) the total reported dollar volume for such Trading Day is not less than $500,000; and (x) at least one bona fide, publicly reported sale of Common Stock during such sessions occurs at a price per share equal to or greater than $2.0265 per share; and (y) the total reported share volume for such Trading Day is no less than 25% greater than the average trading volume over the prior ten (10) Trading Days, excluding the highest-volume day during such period; and (z) least one bona fide, publicly reported sale of Common Stock during such sessions occurs at a price per share equal to or greater than 115% of the official Nasdaq closing price for the immediately preceding Trading Day, then the Leak-Out Percentage shall equal the percentage in column (4) of Schedule A and shall apply only from the time of such sale through the remainder of such Trading Day, regardless of the price of the Common Stock later falls below that threshold. (ii) After the effective date of a registration statement registering the resale of Conversion Shares by Eastward Fund Management LLC , Maxim Group, LLC, and /or their respective Trading Affiliates, the applicable percentage in column (1) of Schedule A (the “ Leak-Out Percentage ”) of the cumulative reported trading volume of the Common Stock from the commencement of that Trading Day’s pre-market session through the time of such sale or disposition. On any Trading Day on which: (w) the total reported dollar volume for such Trading Day is not less than $500,000; and (x) at least one bona fide, publicly reported sale of Common Stock during such sessions occurs at a price per share equal to or greater than $2.0265 per share; and (y) the total reported share volume for such Trading Day is no less than 25% greater than the average trading volume over the prior ten (10) Trading Days, excluding the highest-volume day during such period; and (z) least one bona fide, publicly reported sale of Common Stock during such sessions occurs at a price per share equal to or greater than 115% of the official Nasdaq closing price for the immediately preceding Trading Day, then the Leak-Out Percentage shall equal the percentage in column (2) of Schedule A and shall apply only from the time of such sale through the remainder of such Trading Day, regardless of the price of the Common Stock later falls below that threshold. This limitation covers all shares of Common Stock now held or hereafter acquired, including Conversion Shares and shares from any new funding, except the AP ELOC Shares (as defined below). “Trading Day” for purposes of this Agreement includes the Nasdaq pre-market, regular and post-market sessions on the same New York calendar day (currently 4:00 a.m. through 8:00 p.m., New York time, or the corresponding officially published hours). Volume shall be the consolidated reported share volume during those sessions, as reported by Bloomberg L.P. or, if unavailable, another mutually agreed reliable market-data source, measured consistently for numerator and denominator. No future volume, prior-day volume or unexecuted orders may be used. Notwithstanding the foregoing, shares of Common Stock issued under the Securities Purchase Agreement dated October 27, 2025, as amended, (the “ AP ELOC Shares ”), and sales of such AP ELOC Shares, are excluded from the number of shares of Common Stock such Holder is limited to selling or otherwise disposing of on any given Trading Day. Each Holder shall maintain records reasonably identifying the source of shares sold. (c) Notwithstanding the restrictions set forth in Section 2(b), each Holder may transfer shares of Common Stock without regard to the restrictions set forth herein to (i) any affiliate of such Holder, (ii) any member of such Holder’s immediate family (or a trust formed for the benefit of such Holder or such Holder’s immediate family), (iii) by operation of law, such as pursuant to a qualified domestic order, divorce decree or separation agreement, or (iv) to such Holder’s estate upon death; provided, that in each case the transferee agrees in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement with respect to the transferred shares of Common Stock. Any transfers pursuant to this Section 2(c) shall not effect the maximum number of shares of Common Stock such Holder may sell pursuant to Section 2(b) herein. 3. Remedies . The Company shall have the right to specifically enforce all of the obligations of each Holder under this Agreement (without posting a bond or other security), in addition to recovering damages by reason of any breach by any Holder of any provision of this Agreement and to exercise all other rights granted by law and/or any of the documents related to the acquisition of the shares of Common Stock by such Holder. During the term of this Agreement, the Company may, on reasonable written request to each Holder, inspect records reasonably necessary to verify compliance, including relevant trade confirmations relating to the Common Stock, execution times, prices, volumes and records identifying AP ELOC Shares. Each Holder, shall provide such records within five (5) Business Days of such request, subject to reasonable redaction of unrelated holdings, trades and personal information. The Company shall keep the records confidential and use them solely to verify or enforce this Agreement, and may disclose them only to its professional advisers bound by confidentiality, as required by law, or in an enforcement proceeding subject to reasonable confidentiality protections. For the avoidance of doubt, no Holder is required to pre-clear of trade or permit delay of otherwise lawful conversions, share delivery or sales as a result of this Section 3. 2 4. Further Assurances . Each Party shall do and perform, or cause to be done and performed, all such further acts and things, and shall execute and deliver all such other agreements, certificates, instruments and documents, as each other Party may reasonably request in order to carry out the intent and accomplish the purposes of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby. 5. Notices . All notices, instructions or other communications required or permitted to be given pursuant to this Agreement shall be given in writing and delivered by facsimile, certified mail, return receipt requested or overnight courier by a nationally recognized courier service to the respective address as set forth on the signature page hereto. All notices shall be deemed to be given on the same day if delivered by facsimile, on the following business day if sent by overnight delivery or on the third business day following the date of mailing. 6. Entire Agreement . This Agreement sets forth the entire understanding of the Parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof, and may not be amended except by a written instrument executed by the Parties hereto. This Agreement supersedes prior leak-out restrictions solely with respect to the Holders and its shares of Common Stock. If a Holder’s Exchange Agreement terminates without closing, this Agreement shall not be void ab initio. 7. Governing Law . This Agreement and the terms and conditions set forth herein, shall be governed by and construed solely and exclusively in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Delaware without regard to the conflicts of laws principles thereof. The Parties hereto hereby expressly and irrevocably agree that any suit or proceeding arising directly and/or indirectly pursuant to or under this Agreement shall be brought solely in a federal or state court located in the City of Las Vegas, Clark County, State of Nevada. By its execution hereof, the Parties hereto covenant and irrevocably submit to the in personam jurisdiction of the federal and state courts located in the City of Las Vegas, Clark County, State of Nevada and agree that any process in any such action may be served upon any of them personally, or by certified mail or registered mail upon them or their agent, return receipt requested, with the same full force and effect as if personally served upon them in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Parties hereto expressly and irrevocably waive any claim that any such jurisdiction is not a convenient forum for any such suit or proceeding and any defense or lack of in personam jurisdiction with respect thereto. In the event of any such action or proceeding, the Party prevailing therein shall be entitled to payment from the other Parties hereto of all of its reasonable counsel fees and disbursements. 8. Execution . This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, all of which when taken together shall be considered one and the same agreement and shall become effective when counterparts have been signed by each Party and delivered to each other Party, it being understood that all Parties need not sign the same counterpart. In the event that any signature is delivered by facsimile transmission or by e-mail delivery of a “pdf” format data file, such signature shall create a valid and binding obligation of the Party executing (or on whose behalf such signature is executed) with the same force and effect as if such facsimile or “.pdf” signature page were an original thereof. 9. Severability . In the event any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable for any reason and in any respect, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall in no event affect, prejudice or disturb the validity of the remainder of this Agreement, which shall remain in full force and effect, enforceable in accordance with its terms. R E C I T A L S WHEREAS, KLCC SPV GS1 LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as Borrower (the “ Borrower ”), GS ASL LLC, as Administrative Agent, GOLDMAN SACHS BANK USA as Syndication Agent and as Calculation Agent, U.S. BANK TRUST COMPANY, NATIONAL ASSOCIATION as Collateral Administrator and Collateral Agent, U.S. BANK NATIONAL ASSOCIATION as Collateral Custodian and Securities Intermediary and the Lenders party thereto have entered into that certain credit agreement, dated as of April 20, 2023 (the “ Original Credit Agreement ”, and the Original Credit Agreement as amended and restated by the First Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of October 11, 2024, the First Amendment to First Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of May 5, 2026, the Second Amendment to First Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of July 1, 2026, the Third Amendment to First Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of the date hereof and as may be further amended, supplemented or otherwise modified and in effect from time to time, the “ Credit Agreement ”); WHEREAS, the Limited Guarantor, the Collateral Agent and GS ASL LLC as Administrative Agent (as successor in interest to GOLDMAN SACHS BANK USA) are party to that certain non-recourse carveout guaranty agreement, dated as of April 20, 2023 (the “ Limited Guaranty ,” and the Limited Guaranty as amended by this Amendment and as may be further amended, supplemented or otherwise modified and in effect from time to time, the “ Amended Limited Guaranty ”); WHEREAS, pursuant to and in accordance with Section 5.4 of the Limited Guaranty, the parties hereto desire to amend the Limited Guaranty in certain respects as provided herein; NOW, THEREFORE, based upon the above Recitals, the mutual premises and agreements contained herein and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the undersigned, intending to be legally bound, hereby agree as follows: SECTION 1. Definitions . Except as otherwise defined in this Amendment, terms used herein but not otherwise defined have the meanings given to them in the Limited Guaranty and, if not defined therein, in the Credit Agreement. SECTION 2. Amendments to the Limited Guaranty . From and after the Amendment Effective Date (as defined below), the defined term “Guaranteed Obligations” in Section 1.2 of the Limited Guaranty shall be amended to add the bold, underlined text 1 (indicated textually in the same manner as the following example: underlined text ) to subparagraph (a)(1) as set forth below: (1) willful misconduct, intentional misrepresentation, fraud, theft or other criminal acts by any of the Covered Entities under or in connection with the Transaction Documents or the transactions contemplated thereby; or SECTION 3. Limited Guaranty in Full Force and Effect as Amended . Except as specifically amended hereby, all provisions of the Limited Guaranty shall remain in full force and effect. This Amendment shall not be deemed to expressly or impliedly waive, amend or supplement any provision of the Limited Guaranty other than as expressly set forth herein and shall not constitute a novation of the Limited Guaranty or evidence payment of any portion of the obligations and liabilities arising thereunder. The Limited Guarantor hereby confirms, acknowledges and agrees that the existing security shall continue in full force and effect as a continuing security for all indebtedness, Obligations and liabilities the payment, observance, performance and/or discharge of which is thereby and hereby expressed to be guaranteed and/or secured. The Limited Guarantor acknowledges that the Administrative Agent and the Collateral Agent are relying on the assurances provided herein in entering into this Amendment. SECTION 4. Representations and Warranties . The Limited Guarantor hereby represents and warrants as of the Amendment Effective Date as follows: (a) this Amendment and each other documentation entered into on the date hereof by such party has been duly executed and delivered by it; and (b) this Amendment and the Amended Limited Guaranty (as amended hereby) constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, except as enforceability may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium or similar laws affecting the enforcement of creditors’ rights generally or by general principles of equity. SECTION 5. Conditions to Effectiveness . The amendments set forth above shall become effective as of the date (the “ Amendment Effective Date ”) upon which each of the following conditions precedent shall be satisfied or waived: (a) Execution . The Collateral Agent and the Administrative Agent shall have received executed counterparts of this Amendment. (b) Costs and Expenses . The Borrower shall have paid, on or prior to the Amendment Effective Date, all reasonable and documented out-of-pocket costs and expenses of the Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent incurred in connection with this Amendment payable pursuant to Section 11.2 of the Credit Agreement, including without limitation all reasonable and documented fees and out-of-pocket expenses of counsel to the Collateral Agent and the Administrative Agent incurred in connection with the closing of the transactions contemplated by this Amendment. 2 (c) Certain Documents . The Administrative Agent shall have received, unless otherwise agreed by the Administrative Agent, such instruments, certificates and documents from the Credit Parties as the Administrative Agent and the Lenders shall have reasonably requested. SECTION 6. Miscellaneous . (a) This Amendment is a Transaction Document for all purposes of the Credit Agreement. This Amendment may be executed in any number of counterparts (including by facsimile or electronic mail), and by the different parties hereto on the same or separate counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original instrument but all of which together shall constitute one and the same agreement. (b) The descriptive headings of the various sections of this Amendment are inserted for convenience of reference only and shall not be deemed to affect the meaning or construction of any of the provisions hereof. (c) This Amendment may not be amended or otherwise modified except as provided in the Amended Limited Guaranty. (d) The failure or unenforceability of any provision hereof shall not affect the other provisions of this Amendment. (e) Whenever the context and construction so require, all words used in the singular number herein shall be deemed to have been used in the plural, and vice versa, and the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter and the neuter shall include the masculine and feminine. (f) This Amendment, together with the Amended Limited Guaranty and the other Transaction Documents, represents the final agreement between the parties only with respect to the subject matter expressly covered hereby and may not be contradicted by evidence of prior, contemporaneous or subsequent oral agreements between the parties. There are no unwritten oral agreements between the parties. (g) THIS AMENDMENT AND THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE PARTIES UNDER THIS AMENDMENT SHALL BE GOVERNED BY AND CONSTRUED AND INTERPRETED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK. (h) The Collateral Agent is hereby authorized and directed to execute and deliver this Amendment. text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER AND DIRECTOR AGREEMENT THIS CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER AND DIRECTOR AGREEMENT (the “ Agreement ”), is entered into as of November 2, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), by and between Ocean Capital Acquisition Corporation, a British Virgin Islands business company (the “ Company ”), and Ms. Yiyan Li, an individual (“ Ms. Li ”) (individually, each a “ Party ” and collectively, the “Parties”). WHEREAS, the Company desires to appoint Ms. Li as its Chief Executive Officer, the Chairman of the board of directors of the Company (the “Board”) and a director of the Company, to assure itself of the services of Ms. Li during the term of the Appointment (as defined below). WHEREAS, Ms. Li desires to serve as the Chief Executive Officer, the Chairman of the Board and a director of the Company during the term of the Appointment and upon the terms and conditions of this Agreement. NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises contained herein, the adequacy and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, and intending to be legally bound hereby, the Parties hereby agree as follows: 1. POSITION Ms. Li hereby accepts her appointment as (i) the Chief Executive Officer of the Company, (ii) the Chairman of the Board and (iii) a director of the Company (collectively, the “Appointment”). 2. TERM Subject to the adoption of the applicable Resolution of Directors, the Appointment shall commence on the Effective Date. Ms. Li shall serve as a director of the Company, the Chief Executive Officer and the Chairman of the Board until her resignation from, or removal by the Board from, the applicable office in accordance with Section 6 of this Agreement, the Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association, as amended from time to time (the “Charter Documents”), and applicable law. Ms. Li shall serve as a director for the term specified in the applicable Resolution of Directors. If no term is specified in such resolution, Ms. Li shall hold office as a director until the next annual general meeting of the Company or until her earlier resignation or removal in accordance with Section 6 of this Agreement, the Charter Documents and applicable law. If Ms. Li is appointed to fill a vacancy on the Board, her term as a director shall not exceed the unexpired term of the director whose cessation of office created such vacancy. The period during which Ms. Li serves in any one or more of the foregoing capacities is referred to herein as the “Term.” 3. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (a) In her capacity as Chief Executive Officer, Ms. Li shall perform the duties and exercise the authority customarily incident to the office of chief executive officer of a similarly situated company and shall perform such other duties and exercise such other authority as may from time to time be assigned to her by the Board, in each case consistent with her position as Chief Executive Officer. (b) In her capacity as Chairman of the Board, Ms. Li shall preside over meetings of the Board and perform such other duties and exercise such other authority as may be provided in the Charter Documents or assigned to her by the Board from time to time. (c) In her capacity as a director, Ms. Li shall perform the duties and responsibilities required under applicable British Virgin Islands law, the Charter Documents and the policies of the Company applicable to directors. Ms. Li shall exercise her powers for a proper purpose, act honestly and in good faith in what she believes to be the best interests of the Company, and promptly disclose any interest in a transaction entered into or proposed to be entered into by the Company. 4. NO BREACH OF CONTRACT Ms. Li hereby represents to the Company that: (i) the execution and performance of this Agreement will not materially breach any agreement or obligation binding upon Ms. Li; (ii) Ms. Li is not subject to any obligation that would materially prevent her from performing her duties under this Agreement; and (iii) Ms. Li shall not improperly use or disclose any confidential or proprietary information belonging to any other person in performing such duties. 5. REMUNERATION AND BENEFITS Subject to the consummation of the Company’s initial Business Combination and Ms. Li’s continued service as a director through the closing thereof, Ms. Li shall be entitled to receive from SB Capital Holding Corporation (the “Sponsor”) a shareholder interest in the Sponsor representing an indirect economic interest in 80,000 insider shares held by the Sponsor. Ms. Li shall also be entitled to reimbursement of reasonable and properly documented out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the performance of her duties, subject to the Company’s policies, its organizational documents and applicable law, and solely from funds available outside the Trust Account. 6. CESSATION OF APPOINTMENT (a) Each of Ms. Li’s service as Chief Executive Officer and her service as Chairman of the Board shall cease, with respect to the applicable office, upon the earliest of: (i) her resignation from such office by written notice to the Company; (ii) her removal from such office by the Board in accordance with the Charter Documents and applicable law; (iii) her death; and (iv) the liquidation or dissolution of the Company. Any such resignation shall take effect on the date specified in the applicable notice or, if no date is specified, upon receipt of such notice by the Company. (b) Ms. Li’s service as a director shall cease upon the earliest of: (i) the expiration of the term specified in the Resolution of Members or Resolution of Directors appointing her; (ii) her death; (iii) her resignation as a director in accordance with the Charter Documents; (iv) her removal as a director in accordance with the Charter Documents and applicable British Virgin Islands law; (v) her becoming disqualified from acting as a director under applicable law; and (vi) the liquidation or dissolution of the Company. (c) Any resignation by Ms. Li as a director shall be made by written notice to the Company and shall take effect on the date such notice is received at the office of the Company’s registered agent, or on such later date as may be specified in the notice, in accordance with Regulation 9.6 of the Charter Documents. Any removal of Ms. Li as a director shall be effected only by the corporate action required under the Charter Documents and applicable law. (d) Unless otherwise expressly provided in the applicable Resolution of Directors, resignation notice or other corporate action, the cessation of Ms. Li’s service as Chief Executive Officer shall not, by itself, result in the cessation of her service as Chairman of the Board or as a director, and the cessation of her service as Chairman of the Board shall not, by itself, result in the cessation of her service as Chief Executive Officer or as a director. The cessation of Ms. Li’s service as a director shall automatically result in the cessation of her service as Chairman of the Board but shall not, by itself, result in the cessation of her service as Chief Executive Officer. (e) Upon cessation of Ms. Li’s service in any or all of the foregoing capacities, Ms. Li shall not be entitled to any severance payment, compensation for loss of office, employee benefit, bonus or acceleration of any equity award. 7. CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE (a) Confidentiality and Non-disclosure . The Company and Ms. Li each acknowledge that, in order for the intentions and purposes of this Agreement to be accomplished, Ms. Li hereby agrees at all times during the Term and after her termination, to hold in the strictest confidence, and not to use, except for the benefit of the Company, or to disclose to any person, corporation or other entity without prior written consent of the Company, any Confidential Information. Ms. Li understands that “ Confidential Information ” means any proprietary or confidential information of the Company, its affiliates, or their respective clients, customers or partners, including, without limitation, technical data, trade secrets, research and development information, product plans, services, customer lists and customers, supplier lists and suppliers, software developments, inventions, processes, formulas, technology, designs, hardware configuration information, personnel information, marketing, finances, information about the suppliers, joint ventures, franchisees, distributors and other persons with whom the Company does business, information regarding the skills and compensation of other employees of the Company or other business information disclosed to Ms. Li by or obtained by Ms. Li from the Company, its affiliates, or their respective clients, customers or partners, either directly or indirectly, in writing, orally or otherwise, if specifically indicated to be confidential or reasonably expected to be confidential. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information shall not include information that is generally available and known to the public through no fault of Ms. Li. (b) Company Property . Ms. Li understands that all Company records and materials created, received or maintained by Ms. Li in connection with the performance of her duties are property of the Company and subject to inspection by the Company at any time. Upon termination or at any other time when requested by the Company, Ms. Li will promptly deliver to the Company all documents and materials of any nature pertaining to her work with the Company and will provide written certification of her compliance with this Agreement. Under no circumstances will Ms. Li have, following her termination, in her possession any property of the Company, or any documents or materials or copies thereof containing any Confidential Information. (c) Employer Information . Ms. Li agrees that she has not and will not, during the Term, improperly use or disclose any proprietary information or trade secrets of any current or former employers or other persons or entities with which Ms. Li has an agreement or duty to keep in confidence information acquired by Ms. Li, if any. (d) Third Party Information . Ms. Li recognizes that the Company may have received, and in the future may receive, from third parties their confidential or proprietary information subject to a duty on the Company’s part to maintain the confidentiality of such information and to use it only for certain limited purposes. Ms. Li agrees that she owes the Company and such third parties, during the Term and thereafter, a duty to hold all such confidential or proprietary information in the strictest confidence and not to disclose it to any person or firm and to use it in a manner consistent with, and for the limited purposes permitted by, the Company’s agreement with such third party. This Section 7 shall survive the termination of this Agreement for any reason. In the event Ms. Li breaches this Section 7, the Company shall have the right to seek remedies permissible under applicable law. 8. INDEMNIFICATION The Company agrees to indemnify Ms. Li for her activities as a director and officer of the Company, including in her capacities as Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the Charter Documents, and to cover Ms. Li under any directors’ and officers’ liability insurance obtained by the Company. Further, the Company and Ms. Li agree that, effective as of the date of Ms. Li’s appointment, Ms. Li shall accede to the Company’s existing indemnification arrangements by executing an indemnity agreement substantially in the form of the indemnity agreements dated June 10, 2026 between the Company and its former and current directors and executive officers. 9. ASSIGNMENT This Agreement is personal in its nature and neither of the parties hereto shall, without the consent of the other, assign or transfer this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder; provided, however, that in the event of a Change of Control Transaction, this Agreement shall, subject to the provisions hereof, be binding upon and inure to the benefit of such successor and such successor shall discharge and perform all the promises, covenants, duties, and obligations of the Company hereunder. 10. SEVERABILITY If any provision of this Agreement or the application thereof is held invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Agreement which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application and to this end the provisions of this Agreement are declared to be severable. 11. ENTIRE AGREEMENT This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement and understanding between Ms. Li and the Company solely with respect to the terms of the Appointment and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous oral or written agreements solely concerning such subject matter. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not supersede, amend or limit the Charter Documents, the resolution appointing Ms. Li, any letter agreement relating to the Company’s initial public offering entered into by Ms. Li, any indemnification agreement between Ms. Li and the Company, any applicable D&O insurance policy, or any committee charter or Company policy applicable to Ms. Li. 12. GOVERNING LAW; JURISDICTION This Agreement and the legal relations among the parties shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws rules. To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, the Company and Ms. Li hereby irrevocably and unconditionally: (a) agree that any action or proceeding arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall be brought only in the courts of the British Virgin Islands and not in any other state or federal court in the United States of America or any court in any other country; (b) consent to submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the British Virgin Islands for purposes of any action or proceeding arising out of or in connection with this Agreement; (c) waive any objection to the laying of venue of any such action or proceeding in the courts of the British Virgin Islands; and (d) waive, and agree not to plead or to make, any claim that any such action or proceeding brought in the courts of the British Virgin Islands has been brought in an improper or inconvenient forum, or is subject (in whole or in part) to a jury trial. To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, the parties hereby agree that the mailing of process and other papers in connection with any such action or proceeding in the manner provided by Section 15 or in such other manner as may be permitted by applicable law and the Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, shall be valid and sufficient service thereof. 13. AMENDMENT This Agreement may not be amended, modified or changed (in whole or in part), except by a formal, definitive written agreement expressly referring to this Agreement, which agreement is executed by both of the parties hereto. 14. WAIVER Neither the failure nor any delay on the part of a party to exercise any right, remedy, power or privilege under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right, remedy, power or privilege preclude any other or further exercise of the same or of any right, remedy, power or privilege, nor shall any waiver of any right, remedy, power or privilege with respect to any occurrence be construed as a waiver of such right, remedy, power or privilege with respect to any other occurrence. No waiver shall be effective unless it is in writing and is signed by the party asserted to have granted such waiver. 15. NOTICES All notices, requests, demands and other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given and made if (i) delivered by hand, (ii) otherwise delivered against receipt therefor, or (iii) sent by a recognized courier with next-day or second-day delivery to the last known address of the other party. 16. COUNTERPARTS This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original as against any party whose signature appears thereon, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. This Agreement shall become binding when one or more counterparts hereof, individually or taken together, shall bear the signatures of all of the parties reflected hereon as the signatories. Photographic copies of such signed counterparts may be used in lieu of the originals for any purpose. 17. NO INTERPRETATION AGAINST DRAFTER Each party recognizes that this Agreement is a legally binding contract and acknowledges that such Party has had the opportunity to consult with legal counsel of choice. In any construction of the terms of this Agreement, the same shall not be construed against either party on the basis of that party being the drafter of such terms. text: EX-10.2 3 ex10-2.htm EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 INDEPENDENT DIRECTOR AGREEMENT THIS INDEPENDENT DIRECTOR AGREEMENT (the “ Agreement ”), is entered into as of November 2, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), by and between Ocean Capital Acquisition Corporation, a British Virgin Islands business company (the “ Company ”), and Mr. Stephen J. Posner, an individual (“ Mr. Posner ”) (individually, each a “ Party ” and collectively, the “Parties”). WHEREAS, the Company desires to appoint Mr. Posner as its independent director and a member of each of the Audit Committee, the Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee and the Compensation Committee of the board of directors of the Company (the “Board”) to assure itself of the services of Mr. Posner during the term of the Appointment (as defined below). WHEREAS, Mr. Posner desires to be appointed by the Company as its independent director and a member of each of the Audit Committee, the Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee and the Compensation Committee during the term of the Appointment and upon the terms and conditions of this Agreement. NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises contained herein, the adequacy and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, and intending to be legally bound hereby, the Parties hereby agree as follows: 1. POSITION Mr. Posner hereby accepts the appointment as an independent director of the Company and a member of each of the Audit Committee, the Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee and the Compensation Committee (the “ Appointment ”). 2. TERM Subject to the adoption of the applicable Resolution of Directors, the Appointment shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for the term specified in such resolution. If no term is specified in the applicable resolution, Mr. Posner shall hold office until the next annual general meeting of the Company or until his resignation or removal in accordance with the Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association, as amended from time to time (the “Charter Documents”) and applicable law (the “Term”). If Mr. Posner is appointed to fill a vacancy, the Term shall not exceed the unexpired term of the director whose cessation of office created such vacancy. 3. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (a) Mr. Posner shall perform the duties and responsibilities of a director required under applicable British Virgin Islands law, the Charter Documents, the applicable committee charters and the policies of the Company applicable to directors. Mr. Posner shall exercise his powers for a proper purpose, act honestly and in good faith in what he believes to be the best interests of the Company, and promptly disclose any interest in a transaction entered into or proposed to be entered into by the Company. (b) Mr. Posner shall devote as much working time and attention as necessary to perform his duties at the Company, including duties as a member of each of the Audit Committee, the Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee and the Compensation Committee. (c) Mr. Posner shall promptly disclose to the Company any relationship, interest or change in circumstances that could reasonably affect Mr. Posner’s independence under applicable rules of the New York Stock Exchange or Rule 10A-3 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. 4. NO BREACH OF CONTRACT Mr. Posner hereby represents to the Company that: (i) the execution and performance of this Agreement will not materially breach any agreement or obligation binding upon Mr. Posner; (ii) Mr. Posner is not subject to any obligation that would materially prevent him from performing his duties under this Agreement; and (iii) Mr. Posner shall not improperly use or disclose any confidential or proprietary information belonging to any other person in performing such duties. 5. REMUNERATION AND BENEFITS Subject to the consummation of the Company’s initial Business Combination and Mr. Posner’s continued service as a director through the closing thereof, Mr. Posner shall be entitled to receive from SB Capital Holding Corporation (the “Sponsor”) a shareholder interest in the Sponsor representing an indirect economic interest in 120,000 insider shares held by the Sponsor. Mr. Posner shall also be entitled to reimbursement of reasonable and properly documented out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the performance of his duties, subject to the Company’s policies, its organizational documents and applicable law, and solely from funds available outside the Trust Account. 6. CESSATION OF APPOINTMENT Mr. Posner’s appointment and service shall cease upon the earliest of: (i) the expiration of the term specified in the Resolution of Members or Resolution of Directors appointing Mr. Posner; (ii) Mr. Posner’s death; (iii) Mr. Posner’s resignation in accordance with the Charter Documents; (iv) Mr. Posner’s removal in accordance with the Charter Documents and applicable British Virgin Islands law; (v) Mr. Posner becoming disqualified from acting as a director under applicable law; and (vi) the liquidation or dissolution of the Company. Any resignation by Mr. Posner shall be made by written notice to the Company and shall take effect on the date such notice is received at the office of the Company’s registered agent, or on such later date as may be specified in the notice, in accordance with Regulation 9.6 of the Charter Documents. Any removal of Mr. Posner shall be effected only by the corporate action required under the Charter Documents and applicable law. Upon cessation of Mr. Posner’s appointment, Mr. Posner shall not be entitled to any severance payment, compensation for loss of office, employee benefit, bonus or acceleration of any equity award. 7. CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE (a) Confidentiality and Non-disclosure . The Company and Mr. Posner each acknowledge that, in order for the intentions and purposes of this Agreement to be accomplished, Mr. Posner hereby agrees at all times during the Term and after his termination, to hold in the strictest confidence, and not to use, except for the benefit of the Company, or to disclose to any person, corporation or other entity without prior written consent of the Company, any Confidential Information. Mr. Posner understands that “ Confidential Information ” means any proprietary or confidential information of the Company, its affiliates, or their respective clients, customers or partners, including, without limitation, technical data, trade secrets, research and development information, product plans, services, customer lists and customers, supplier lists and suppliers, software developments, inventions, processes, formulas, technology, designs, hardware configuration information, personnel information, marketing, finances, information about the suppliers, joint ventures, franchisees, distributors and other persons with whom the Company does business, information regarding the skills and compensation of other employees of the Company or other business information disclosed to Mr. Posner by or obtained by Mr. Posner from the Company, its affiliates, or their respective clients, customers or partners, either directly or indirectly, in writing, orally or otherwise, if specifically indicated to be confidential or reasonably expected to be confidential. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information shall not include information that is generally available and known to the public through no fault of Mr. Posner. (b) Company Property . Mr. Posner understands that all Company records and materials created, received or maintained by Mr. Posner in connection with the performance of his duties are property of the Company and subject to inspection by the Company at any time. Upon termination or at any other time when requested by the Company, Mr. Posner will promptly deliver to the Company all documents and materials of any nature pertaining to his work with the Company and will provide written certification of his compliance with this Agreement. Under no circumstances will Mr. Posner have, following his termination, in his possession any property of the Company, or any documents or materials or copies thereof containing any Confidential Information. (c) Employer Information . Mr. Posner agrees that he has not and will not, during the Term, improperly use or disclose any proprietary information or trade secrets of any current or former employers or other persons or entities with which Mr. Posner has an agreement or duty to keep in confidence information acquired by Mr. Posner, if any. (d) Third Party Information . Mr. Posner recognizes that the Company may have received, and in the future may receive, from third parties their confidential or proprietary information subject to a duty on the Company’s part to maintain the confidentiality of such information and to use it only for certain limited purposes. Mr. Posner agrees that he owes the Company and such third parties, during the Term and thereafter, a duty to hold all such confidential or proprietary information in the strictest confidence and not to disclose it to any person or firm and to use it in a manner consistent with, and for the limited purposes permitted by, the Company’s agreement with such third party. This Section 7 shall survive the termination of this Agreement for any reason. In the event Mr. Posner breaches this Section 7, the Company shall have the right to seek remedies permissible under applicable law. 8. INDEMNIFICATION The Company agrees to indemnify Mr. Posner for his activities as a director of the Company to the fullest extent permitted by law, and to cover Mr. Posner under any directors’ and officers’ liability insurance obtained by the Company. At or before the closing of the Company’s initial Business Combination, the Company shall, at its own expense, purchase a six-year extended reporting period endorsement to its directors’ and officers’ liability insurance policy, providing coverage for Mr. Posner and the other insured directors and officers for a period of six years following such closing in respect of claims arising from acts or omissions occurring at or prior to such closing. The Company’s obligations under this paragraph shall survive the cessation of Mr. Posner’s appointment and the termination of this Agreement. Further, the Company and Mr. Posner agree that, effective as of the date of Mr. Posner’s appointment, Mr. Posner shall accede to the Company’s existing indemnification arrangements by executing an indemnity agreement substantially in the form of the indemnity agreements dated June 10, 2026 between the Company and its former and current directors and executive officers. 9. ASSIGNMENT This Agreement is personal in its nature and neither of the parties hereto shall, without the consent of the other, assign or transfer this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder; provided, however, that in the event of a Change of Control Transaction, this Agreement shall, subject to the provisions hereof, be binding upon and inure to the benefit of such successor and such successor shall discharge and perform all the promises, covenants, duties, and obligations of the Company hereunder. 10. SEVERABILITY If any provision of this Agreement or the application thereof is held invalid, the invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Agreement which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application and to this end the provisions of this Agreement are declared to be severable. 11. ENTIRE AGREEMENT This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement and understanding between Mr. Posner and the Company solely with respect to the terms of the Appointment and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous oral or written agreements solely concerning such subject matter. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not supersede, amend or limit the Charter Documents, the resolution appointing Mr. Posner, any letter agreement relating to the Company’s initial public offering entered into by Mr. Posner, any indemnification agreement between Mr. Posner and the Company, any applicable D&O insurance policy, or any committee charter or Company policy applicable to Mr. Posner. 12. GOVERNING LAW; JURISDICTION This Agreement and the legal relations among the parties shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws rules. To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, including its breach, termination or validity, shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association in accordance with its Commercial Arbitration Rules. The arbitration shall be conducted before one arbitrator appointed in accordance with such rules. The seat of arbitration shall be New York City, New York. The arbitral award shall be final and binding on the Company and Mr. Posner, and judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the parties hereby agree that service of process and other papers in connection with any court proceeding relating to the arbitration or the arbitral award may be made in the manner provided by Section 15 or in any other manner permitted by applicable law. 13. AMENDMENT This Agreement may not be amended, modified or changed (in whole or in part), except by a formal, definitive written agreement expressly referring to this Agreement, which agreement is executed by both of the parties hereto. 14. WAIVER Neither the failure nor any delay on the part of a party to exercise any right, remedy, power or privilege under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right, remedy, power or privilege preclude any other or further exercise of the same or of any right, remedy, power or privilege, nor shall any waiver of any right, remedy, power or privilege with respect to any occurrence be construed as a waiver of such right, remedy, power or privilege with respect to any other occurrence. No waiver shall be effective unless it is in writing and is signed by the party asserted to have granted such waiver. 15. NOTICES All notices, requests, demands and other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given and made if (i) delivered by hand, (ii) otherwise delivered against receipt therefor, or (iii) sent by a recognized courier with next-day or second-day delivery to the last known address of the other party. 16. COUNTERPARTS This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original as against any party whose signature appears thereon, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. This Agreement shall become binding when one or more counterparts hereof, individually or taken together, shall bear the signatures of all of the parties reflected hereon as the signatories. Photographic copies of such signed counterparts may be used in lieu of the originals for any purpose. 17. NO INTERPRETATION AGAINST DRAFTER Each party recognizes that this Agreement is a legally binding contract and acknowledges that such Party has had the opportunity to consult with legal counsel of choice. In any construction of the terms of this Agreement, the same shall not be construed against either party on the basis of that party being the drafter of such terms.
