DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION Unless otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms which are used herein shall have the meanings assigned to such terms in Section 1.1 ( Certain defined terms ) of the Receivables Transfer Agreement. The principles of interpretation set forth in Section 1.2 ( Other terms ) and Section 1.3 ( Computation of time periods ) of the Receivables Transfer Agreement shall apply to this Amendment as if fully set forth herein. 2. AMENDMENT OF THE RECEIVABLES TRANSFER AGREEMENT (a) With effect as of the later of (i) the Thirty-First Amendment Effective Date (as such term is defined in Section 8 ( Conditions Precedent )), and (ii) so long as no Facility Termination Event or Potential Facility Termination Event shall have occurred and be continuing, 12:01 a.m. (New York City time) on December 14, 2026 (the later of the dates described in clauses (i) and (ii) shall be referred to herein as the “ Extension Effective Date ”), the Receivables Transfer Agreement shall be amended as set forth herein: (i) In Section 1.1 ( Definitions ), the definition of “Original Termination Date” shall be amended and restated in its entirety as follows: “ Original Termination Date ” means December 13, 2027. 2 (b) With effect from the Thirty-First Amendment Effective Date (as such term is defined in Section 8 ( Conditions Precedent )), the Receivables Transfer Agreement shall be further amended as set forth herein: (i) Schedule 1 ( Purchaser Groups ) shall be deleted and replaced with Exhibit A hereto. (ii) Schedule 2 ( Address and Notice Information ) shall be deleted and replaced with Exhibit B hereto. (iii) Schedule 5 ( Facility Accounts and Facility Account Banks ) shall be deleted and replaced with Exhibit C hereto. (iv) Schedule 9 ( Excluded Obligors ) shall be deleted and replaced with Exhibit D hereto. (c) The Parties hereto, including but not limited to each Committed Purchaser, agrees, acknowledges and consents to the extension of the Original Termination Date to December 13, 2027 as a Fundamental Change. 3. REPRESENTATIONS Each of the Seller, the Master Servicer and the Performance Undertaking Provider represents and warrants to the other Parties hereto that, after giving effect to this Amendment, the extension of the Original Termination Date, the amendments to the Dutch RPA and the amendments to the French RPA, each of its representations and warranties set forth in the Receivables Transfer Agreement, as such representations and warranties apply to such Person, is true and correct in all material respects on and as of the Thirty-First Amendment Effective Date, the Extension Effective Date, the BNABV Dutch Merger Amendment Effective Date and the French Originator Merger Amendment Effective Date as though made on and as of such date except for representations and warranties stated to refer to a specific earlier date, in which case such representations and warranties are true and correct as of such earlier date. 4. CONSENT TO AMENDMENT OF FRENCH RPA (a) Within thirty (30) days after the effective date of the French Originator Merger, the Seller shall procure that the French Originator deliver a written notice (which may be in the form of an email) to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent confirming that the French Originator Merger is valid and effective (the “ French Originator Merger Amendment Effective Date ”). (b) The Parties hereto each agree, acknowledge and consent to Schedule 1 ( Seller Information ) to the French RPA being deleted and replaced with Exhibit F hereto as of the later of (i) the Thirty-First Amendment Effective Date and (ii) the French Originator Merger Amendment Effective Date. 3 5. CONSENT TO BNABV DUTCH MERGER AND BOTLEK DUTCH MERGER AND AMENDMENT OF DUTCH RPA, EACH DUTCH ACCOUNT SECURITY AGREEMENT AND EACH OTHER TRANSACTION DOCUMENT (a) Within thirty (30) days after the effective date of the BNABV Dutch Merger, (i) the Seller shall procure that BNABV shall deliver a written notice to the Seller, the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent confirming that the BNABV Dutch Merger is valid and effective and as a result of the BNABV Dutch Merger, BNABV agrees and acknowledges that (x) all of the rights and obligations of the Existing Dutch Originator under the Dutch RPA, each Dutch Account Security Agreement and each other Transaction Document to which the Existing Dutch Originator is a party transferred to BNABV under universal title and by operation of Dutch law, (y) the Existing Dutch Originator ceased to exist and (z) BNABV is bound by all rights and obligations of the Existing Dutch Originator under the Dutch RPA, each Dutch Account Security Agreement and each other Transaction Document to which it is a party; (ii) the Seller shall file (x) a UCC-3 amendment to amend the existing UCC-1 financing statement that has been filed against Bunge Netherlands B.V. in connection with the Dutch RPA and (y) a UCC-1 financing statement against BNABV in connection with the Dutch RPA, in each case to reflect the BNABV Dutch Merger and shall provide filed copies of the same to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent; (iii) the Seller shall procure that BNABV shall create a supplemental right of pledge in respect of any Dutch Pledged Collection Account (as defined in the Dutch Account Pledge Agreement entered into by the Existing Dutch Originator) substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F to be registered with the Dutch tax authorities with evidence of such registration delivered to the Administrative Agent, and notified to each relevant Account Bank (including JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.); (iv) Reed Smith LLP, special U.S. counsel for the Master Servicer and BNABV shall deliver a legal opinion in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent, that the Seller has a perfected security interest in all Receivables and Related Security purported to be sold by BNABV to the Seller under the Dutch RPA and that the provisions of the Dutch RPA and the form of financing statement naming BNABV as debtor filed in Washington D.C. are sufficient in form to establish a legal, valid, binding and enforceable transfer of all of BNABV’s rights, title and interest in and to the Receivables and the Related Property from BNABV to the Seller (and the Administrative Agent as assignee thereof); and (v) Clifford Chance LLP, special Dutch counsel for BNABV shall deliver a legal opinion in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent setting out the transfer by universal title of the Existing Dutch Originator’s rights and obligations under the Dutch RPA and the Dutch Account Security Agreement, the validity and enforceability of the supplemental pledge and the capacity of BNABV to execute such supplemental pledge (the later of the Thirty-First Amendment Effective Date and the date on which clauses (i)-(v) above have been satisfied, so long as no Facility Termination Event or Potential Facility Termination Event 4 shall have occurred and be continuing, shall be referred to herein as the “ BNABV Dutch Merger Amendment Effective Date ”). (b) The Parties hereto each agree, acknowledge and consent to the BNABV Dutch Merger and the Botlek Dutch Merger. For purposes of section 9.1(b) of the Dutch RPA, clause 12.8 of the Dutch Account Pledge Agreement and clause 7.2 of the Dutch Declaration of Trust, the Parties hereto agree that, as of the BNABV Dutch Merger Amendment Effective Date, all references in the Receivables Transfer Agreement, the Dutch RPA, each Dutch Account Security Agreement and each other Transaction Document to: “Bunge Netherlands B.V.” shall be deleted and replaced with references to "Bunge Netherlands Agri B.V." "having its official seat ( statutaire zetel ) in Amsterdam, the Netherlands and registered with the Dutch trade register under number 66808006" shall be deleted and replaced with references to "having its official seat ( statutaire zetel ) in Rotterdam, the Netherlands and registered with the Dutch trade register under number 24138640" "having its official seat in Amsterdam, the Netherlands and having its registered office address at Coenhavenweg 3 (1013BK) Amsterdam, the Netherlands, registered with the Trade Register under number 66808006" shall be deleted and replaced with references to "having its official seat in Rotterdam, the Netherlands and having its registered office address at Blaak 31 (3011GA)Rotterdam, the Netherlands, registered with the Trade Register under number 24138640". (c) Within thirty (30) days after the effective date of the Botlek Dutch Merger, the Seller shall procure that BNABV shall deliver a written notice (which may be in the form of an email) to the Seller, the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent confirming that the Botlek Dutch Merger is valid and effective (the later of the Thirty-First Amendment Effective Date and the date on which such written notice has been delivered shall be referred to herein as the “ Botlek Dutch Merger Amendment Effective Date ”). (d) The Parties hereto each agree, acknowledge and consent to Schedule 1 ( Seller Information ) to the Dutch RPA being deleted and replaced with Exhibit E hereto as of the later of the Botlek Dutch Merger Amendment Effective Date and the BNABV Dutch Merger Amendment Effective Date. (e) The Parties hereto waive any further notice or consent requirements in respect of the BNABV Dutch Merger and the Botlek Dutch Merger. 6. CONTINUANCE 5 The Parties hereby confirm that the provisions of the Receivables Transfer Agreement and the other Transaction Documents shall continue in full force and effect, subject only to the amendments effected thereto by this Amendment. 7. FURTHER ASSURANCE The Parties shall, upon request of the Administrative Agent, and at the cost of the Seller, do all such acts and things necessary or desirable to give effect to the amendments effected or to be effected by this Amendment. Each of the Parties thereto hereby ratifies and confirms each of the Transaction Documents to which it is a party. 8. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT This Amendment shall become effective as of 12:01 a.m. (New York City time) on November 1, 2026 upon the notice from the Administrative Agent to the Seller and Purchasers that the Administrative Agent has received, in each case in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent, the following, duly executed by all parties thereto (the “ Thirty-First Amendment Effective Date ”); provided , that the Administrative Agent may, acting on the instructions of the Purchasers, waive any of the following conditions precedent: (a) this Amendment; (b) the Reaffirmation of Performance Undertaking, dated as of the date hereof, made by the Performance Undertaking Provider for the benefit of the Administrative Agent; (c) a notice from the French Originator to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent, dated on a date at least twenty (20) Business Days prior to the date hereof, regarding the French Originator Merger; (d) a notice from the Existing Dutch Originator to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent, dated on a date at least twenty (20) Business Days prior to the date hereof, regarding (i) the merger of Bunge Netherlands B.V. into BNABV and (ii) the merger of Botlek into BNABV; (e) summaries of the due diligence review of sample sales contracts of Viterra France and BNABV; (f) a certificate of a manager of the Seller, dated as of the date hereof, and certifying (i) that attached thereto is a true and complete copy of the Organizational Documents (including all amendments or other modifications thereto) of the Seller, as in effect as of the date hereof, (ii) that attached thereto is a true and complete copy of the resolutions of the Board of Directors (or committee thereof), directors or, to the extent required, shareholders and (to the extent applicable) the request for advice and the positive advice from the works council that has 6 jurisdiction over such transaction, as the case may be, of the Seller authorizing the execution, delivery and performance of this Amendment and the other Transaction Documents to which it is a party and the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, and that such resolutions have not been amended, modified, revoked or rescinded and are in full force and effect, and (iii) the authority and specimen signature of each officer executing this Amendment and each other Transaction Documents or any other document delivered in connection herewith on behalf of the Seller; (g) an extract, dated as of a recent date, from the Trade Register or other appropriate authority of the Seller’s jurisdiction of organization; (h) a certificate of a secretary of the Performance Undertaking Provider, dated as of the date hereof, and certifying (i) that attached thereto is a true and complete copy of the Organizational Documents (including all amendments or other modifications thereto) of the Performance Undertaking Provider, as in effect as of the date hereof, (ii) that attached thereto is a true and complete copy of the resolutions of the Board of Directors (or committee thereof) of the Performance Undertaking Provider authorizing the execution, delivery and performance of this Amendment and the other Transaction Documents to which it is a party and the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby, and that such resolutions have not been amended, modified, revoked or rescinded and are in full force and effect, and (iii) the authority and specimen signature of each officer executing this Amendment and each other Transaction Documents or any other document delivered in connection herewith on behalf of the Performance Undertaking Provider; (i) an extract, dated as of a recent date, from the Commercial Register of Canton of Geneva, with respect to the Performance Undertaking Provider; (j) a legal opinion of Homburger, special Swiss counsel for the Performance Undertaking Provider, in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent; (k) a legal opinion of Clifford Chance LLP, special Dutch counsel for the Seller, in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent; (l) legal opinions of Reed Smith LLP, special U.S. counsel for the Seller, the Master Servicer and the Performance Undertaking Provider, in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent, including opinions with respect to the due authorization, execution and delivery of, and the validity and enforceability of, this Amendment and the other Transaction Documents governed by New York law; 7 (m) evidence that Clifford Chance LLP, special Dutch counsel for the Seller, has the information required in order to promptly make a notification in the Netherlands in accordance with Article 7(1)(g)(V) of the Securitisation Regulation; (n) confirmation by each Purchaser Agent that it has received all internal confirmations (including, to the extent required, any diligence (commercial and legal), tax, compliance, 'know-your-customer' and/or credit committee) required for purposes of this Amendment or any of the other Transaction Documents described in this Section 8 ; (o) an updated transaction summary, in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent; (p) an updated transaction summary, in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each Purchaser Agent; and (q) provision by PCS of a "no objection letter" to the Administrative Agent. 9. NOTICES, ETC. All communications and notices provided for hereunder shall be provided in the manner described in Schedule 2 ( Address and Notice Information ) to the Receivables Transfer Agreement. 10. EXECUTION IN COUNTERPARTS This Amendment may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which when so executed shall be deemed to be an original and all of which when taken together shall constitute one and the same agreement. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Amendment by facsimile or by electronic file in a format that is accessible by the recipient shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart of this Amendment. 11. GOVERNING LAW; SUBMISSION TO JURISDICTION (a) This Amendment shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of the state of New York. (b) Each of the Parties hereto hereby irrevocably and unconditionally submits, for itself and its property, to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of the State of New York sitting in the Borough of Manhattan and of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, and any appellate court from any thereof, in any action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Amendment. Each Party hereto hereby irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent that it may legally do so, the defense of an inconvenient forum to the maintenance of such action or proceeding. Each Party hereto agrees that a final 8 judgment in any such action or proceeding shall be conclusive and may be enforced in other jurisdictions by suit on the judgment or in any other manner provided by law. (c) TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, EACH OF THE PARTIES HERETO WAIVES ITS RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY OF ANY CLAIM OR CAUSE OF ACTION BASED UPON OR ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AMENDMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY, IN ANY ACTION, PROCEEDING OR OTHER LITIGATION OF ANY TYPE BROUGHT BY ANY OF THE PARTIES AGAINST ANY OTHER PARTY OR PARTIES, WHETHER WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACT CLAIMS, TORT CLAIMS OR OTHERWISE. EACH OF THE PARTIES HERETO AGREES THAT ANY SUCH CLAIM OR CAUSE OF ACTION SHALL BE TRIED BY A COURT TRIAL WITHOUT A JURY. WITHOUT LIMITING THE FOREGOING, EACH OF THE PARTIES HERETO FURTHER AGREES THAT ITS RESPECTIVE RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IS WAIVED BY OPERATION OF THIS SECTION AS TO ANY ACTION, COUNTERCLAIM OR OTHER PROCEEDING WHICH SEEKS, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, TO CHALLENGE THE VALIDITY OR ENFORCEABILITY OF THIS AMENDMENT OR ANY PROVISION HEREOF. 12. NO PROCEEDING; LIMITED RECOURSE (a) Each of the Parties hereto hereby agrees that (i) it will not institute against any Conduit Purchaser any proceeding of the type referred to in the definition of Event of Bankruptcy until there shall have elapsed two years plus one day since the Final Payout Date and (ii) notwithstanding anything contained herein or in any other Transaction Document to the contrary, the obligations of the Conduit Purchasers under the Transaction Documents are solely the corporate obligations of the Conduit Purchasers and shall be payable solely to the extent of funds which are received by the Conduit Purchasers pursuant to the Transaction Documents and available for such payment in accordance with the terms of the Transaction Documents and shall be non-recourse other than with respect to such available funds and, without limiting this Section 11 , if ever and until such time as any Conduit Purchaser has sufficient funds to pay such obligation shall not constitute a claim against such Conduit Purchaser. (b) No recourse under any obligation, covenant or agreement of any Committed Purchaser or Conduit Purchaser contained in this Amendment or any other Transaction Document shall be had against any incorporator, stockholder, officer, director, member, manager, employee or agent of such Committed Purchaser or Conduit Purchaser by the enforcement of any assessment or by any legal or equitable proceeding, by virtue of any statute or otherwise; it being expressly agreed and understood that this Amendment and the other Transaction Documents 9 are solely a corporate obligation of such Committed Purchaser or Conduit Purchaser, and that no personal liability whatever shall attach to or be incurred by any incorporator, stockholder, officer, director, member, manager, employee or agent of such Committed Purchaser or Conduit Purchaser or any of them under or by reason of any of the obligations, covenants or agreements of such Committed Purchaser or Conduit Purchaser contained in this Amendment or any other Transaction Document, or implied therefrom, and that any and all personal liability for breaches by such Committed Purchaser or Conduit Purchaser of any of such obligations, covenants or agreements, either at common law or at equity, or by statute, rule or regulation, of every such incorporator, stockholder, officer, director, member, manager, employee or agent is hereby expressly waived as a condition of and in consideration for the execution of this Amendment; provided that the foregoing shall not relieve any such Person from any liability it might otherwise have as a result of fraudulent actions taken or fraudulent omissions made by them. [Signature pages follow.] 10 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Amendment as of the day and year first above written. title: Rising Dragon Acquisition Corp.
text: EX-10.1 2 ea031053501ex10-1.htm TERMINATION AGREEMENT, DATED OCTOBER 30, 2026, BY AND AMONG RISING DRAGON ACQUISITION CORP., XPAND BOOM TECHNOLOGY INC., XPAND BOOM SOLUTIONS INC., HZJL CAYMAN LIMITED, XB B LIMITED AND BIN XIONG Exhibit 10.1 Rising Dragon Acquisition Corp. No. 604, Yixing Road Wanbolin District, Taiyuan City Shanxi Province, People’s Republic of China October 30, 2026 VIA OVERNIGHT DELIVERY AND EMAIL HZJL Cayman Limited 18th Floor, Block B, Yuanlun Building, No. 350 Qifei Road Binjiang District, Hangzhou City, People’s Republic of China Attention: Bin Xiong Email: xiongb@pku.edu.cn XB B Limited and Bin Xiong, as Principal Shareholder Representative 18th Floor, Block B, Yuanlun Building, No. 350 Qifei Road Binjiang District, Hangzhou City, People’s Republic of China Attention: Bin Xiong Email: xiongb@pku.edu.cn Re: Termination of Agreement and Plan of Merger Ladies and Gentlemen: Pursuant to Section 13.1(b) of that certain Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of January 27, 2025 (as amended, modified or supplemented from time to time, the “Merger Agreement”), by and among HZJL Cayman Limited, a Cayman Islands exempted company (the “Company”), XB B Limited, a British Virgin Islands business company (the “Principal Shareholder”), Bin Xiong, solely in his capacity as the shareholder of the Principal Shareholder (the “Principal Shareholder Representative”), Rising Dragon Acquisition Corp., a Cayman Islands exempted company (“Parent”), Xpand Boom Technology Inc., a Cayman Islands exempted company (the “Purchaser”), and Xpand Boom Solutions Inc., a Cayman Islands exempted company (“Merger Sub”) (each individually referred to as a “Party” and collectively, the “Parties”), the Merger Agreement may be terminated at any time by mutual written consent of the Company and Parent duly authorized by each of their respective boards of directors. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings ascribed to them in the Merger Agreement. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Merger Agreement, the Parties agree as follows: 1. Acting pursuant to Section 13.1(b) of the Merger Agreement and with due authorization from their respective boards of directors, Parent and the Company hereby terminate the Merger Agreement, including provisions of the Merger Agreement which by their terms would otherwise have survived the termination of the Merger Agreement, and each of the other Parties hereby consents to such termination, effective as of 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the date first written above (the “Termination Date”); provided, however, that the provisions of Article XII (Dispute Resolution) and Article XIV (Miscellaneous) (including Section 14.14 (Waiver)) of the Merger Agreement shall survive the termination of the Merger Agreement and continue in full force and effect. 2. With respect to the Additional Agreements and the Support Agreements, the Parties acknowledge and agree as follows: (a) the Company Shareholders Lock-up Agreements and the Registration Rights Agreement, each of which was contemplated to be entered into at or in connection with the Closing, have not been executed or become effective, and no Party or other Person shall have any obligation to execute or deliver any such agreement or any other Additional Agreement; (b) to the extent any Additional Agreement has been executed, it is hereby terminated as of the Termination Date without further action on the part of the parties thereto, including any provisions thereof which by their terms would otherwise survive termination, except that nothing herein shall terminate or otherwise affect any Non-disclosure and Non-solicitation Agreement or Non-Compete Agreement entered into between any member of the Company Group and any Key Personnel pursuant to Section 8.4 of the Merger Agreement, which shall remain in effect solely as between the parties thereto in accordance with its terms, and no Purchaser Party shall have any right or obligation thereunder; and (c) each support agreement entered into by any Company Shareholder prior to the execution of the Merger Agreement as described in Recital I thereof (each, a “Support Agreement”) shall terminate as of the Termination Date in accordance with its terms, and, to the extent any Party is a party to or a beneficiary of any Support Agreement, such Party hereby agrees that such Support Agreement is terminated as to it as of the Termination Date and irrevocably waives all of its rights thereunder. The Company shall, promptly following the Termination Date, notify each Company Shareholder party to a Support Agreement of the termination of the Merger Agreement and of such Support Agreement. 3. No Party shall issue a press release or similar formal public statement relating to the Merger Agreement or the termination of the Merger Agreement (the “Public Announcement”) without all Parties’ prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. The foregoing does not apply to disclosures by a Party (a) to the extent obtaining the other Parties’ prior written consent is prohibited by Law or (b) to the extent required by Law or pursuant to the rules or regulations of any securities exchange, in response to a request for information from an Authority, or as required as part of a periodic regulatory filing (including any Parent SEC Document). The Parties agree that the press release attached hereto as Exhibit A and the Current Report on Form 8-K to be filed by Parent with the SEC reporting the termination of the Merger Agreement shall be deemed to have been consented to by all Parties for purposes of this paragraph 3. 4. No Party shall, and no Party shall cause or permit any officer or Affiliate to, disparage any other Party in any manner whatsoever whether in writing, orally or otherwise in any media. Without limitation, each Party shall not engage in any vilification of any other Party, and each Party shall refrain from making any false, negative, critical or disparaging statements concerning any other Party, including those pertaining to management style, methods of doing business, the quality of products and services, role in the community, or treatment of employees. Notwithstanding the foregoing, and for the purpose of clarification, no Party shall be deemed to be in breach of this paragraph 4 (a) based on or as a result of such Party’s making of any disclosure or provision of information to the extent (i) required by Law or pursuant to the rules or regulations of any securities exchange (including in any Parent SEC Document) or (ii) in response to a request for information from an Authority, or (b) based on or as a result of such Party’s making of any statement or claim, or such Party’s provision of information, in or pursuant to any Action to the extent such statement or claim is made, or such information is provided, in furtherance of or with respect to any right, claim, or matter not waived, released or discharged pursuant to paragraph 6 hereof. 2 5. No Party shall make, share, publish or communicate to any Person, in any public or private forum or through any medium, any information whatsoever, directly or indirectly, about another Party, the Merger Agreement, the termination of the Merger Agreement or related transactions or matters obtained or derived in connection with the Merger Agreement or its termination, without the affected Party’s express written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, and for the purpose of clarification, no Party shall be deemed to be in breach of this paragraph 5 (a) based on or as a result of such Party’s making of any disclosure or provision of information to the extent (i) required by Law or pursuant to the rules or regulations of any securities exchange (including in any Parent SEC Document) or (ii) in response to a request for information from an Authority, or (b) based on or as a result of such Party’s making of any statement or claim, or such Party’s provision of information, in or pursuant to any Action to the extent such statement or claim is made, or such information is provided, in furtherance of or with respect to any right, claim, or matter not waived, released or discharged pursuant to paragraph 6 hereof. 6. To the fullest extent permitted by Law, each Party irrevocably, unconditionally and completely waives, and releases and forever discharges each other Party (and any shareholder, director, officer, employee, Affiliate, agent, consultant or representative of such other Party) from, all claims, damages, costs and expenses, whether known or unknown or due or owing in the past, present or future, arising from any matter concerning, based upon, in connection with, or relating to, the Merger Agreement, the Additional Agreements or the Support Agreements, or the termination thereof or of the transactions contemplated thereby; provided, that (a) for the purpose of clarification, the foregoing waiver, release and discharge shall not apply to or otherwise affect the rights of any Party under Article XII or Article XIV of the Merger Agreement to the extent (and for so long as) such provisions survive the termination of the Merger Agreement pursuant to this letter agreement, or the rights of any member of the Company Group under any agreement preserved pursuant to paragraph 2(b), and (b) nothing in this letter agreement shall relieve any Party from liability for such Party’s willful breach of its covenants or agreements in the Merger Agreement or its intentional fraud or willful misconduct prior to the termination of the Merger Agreement. Each Party confirms that it has not assigned to any third party any claims that such Party has waived, released or discharged pursuant to this paragraph 6. 7. Each of the Company, the Principal Shareholder and the Principal Shareholder Representative hereby acknowledges and reaffirms that the waiver set forth in Section 14.14 of the Merger Agreement survives the termination of the Merger Agreement, and that none of them has, or shall have, any right, title, interest or claim of any kind in or to any monies in the Trust Account or any distributions therefrom, and that none of them shall make any claim against the Trust Account, regardless of whether such claim arises as a result of, in connection with or relating in any way to the Merger Agreement, this letter agreement or the termination of the Merger Agreement. 8. This letter agreement will be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the Laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to the conflict of laws principles thereof. Any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this letter agreement shall be resolved in accordance with Article XII of the Merger Agreement, which is incorporated herein by reference, mutatis mutandis. This letter agreement may be executed and delivered (including by facsimile, portable document format (.pdf) transmission or other electronic signature) in one or more counterparts, and by the different Parties in separate counterparts, each of which when executed shall be deemed to be an original but all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same agreement. 3 9. Each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates to, execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, conveyances, and assurances and take such further actions as may be required to carry out the provisions of this letter agreement and give effect to the transactions contemplated hereby. 10. The Parties acknowledge that this letter agreement shall be binding on and inure to the benefit of their respective successors and assigns. 11. Survival and Payment Arrangement of Subject Promissory Notes . (a) Definitions . For purposes of this paragraph 11: (i) “Maker” means Parent; (ii) “Payee” means SZG Limited, as designee of the Company, and Aurora Beacon LLC, also as designee of the Company; each a “Payee” and collectively the “Payees”, together with their respective permitted successors and assigns under the Subject Promissory Notes; (iii) “Subject Promissory Notes” means all unsecured promissory notes issued by the Maker in favor of each Payee, including (1) the promissory notes issued by the Maker in favor of SZG Limited as set forth on Schedule 1.1 hereto, and (2) all promissory notes of the same series issued by the Maker in favor of Aurora Beacon LLC; in each case, in the principal amount and as of the date set forth in the applicable note; and (iv) “Subsequent Business Combination” means any initial business combination transaction consummated by the Maker with any target business after the Termination Date. (b) Survival of Subject Promissory Notes . Notwithstanding (i) any term of any Subject Promissory Note to the contrary that would provide for termination upon termination of the Merger Agreement, (ii) paragraph 2 of this letter agreement, or (iii) the general release set forth in paragraph 6 of this letter agreement, the Subject Promissory Notes shall not be terminated, cancelled or discharged as of the Termination Date, and shall remain in full force and effect in accordance with their respective terms, as modified solely by this paragraph 11. The general release under paragraph 6 shall not apply to the payment obligations under the Subject Promissory Notes, except as expressly set forth in clause (d) below. (c) Payment Trigger . The entire outstanding principal balance of each Subject Promissory Note shall be due and payable solely on the closing date of the first Subsequent Business Combination consummated by the Maker. No principal shall be due and payable under any Subject Promissory Note prior to such closing date. (d) Automatic Termination Without Payment . Each Subject Promissory Note shall be automatically deemed terminated, cancelled and discharged in full, and no principal or other amounts shall be due or payable thereunder, upon the earliest occurrence of either of the following: (i) the Maker fails to consummate any Subsequent Business Combination; or (ii) any proposed Subsequent Business Combination fails to close for reasons not attributable to the Maker. (e) No Other Modification . Except as expressly modified by this paragraph 11, all other terms, conditions and provisions of each Subject Promissory Note shall remain unchanged and in full force and effect. 4 Kindly signify your agreement by signing this letter agreement in the space provided below. title: Alphega Innovations Corp
text: EX-10.1 2 alpga_ex10-1.htm STRATEGIC COOPERATION AGREEMENT Strategic Cooperation Agreement STRATEGIC COOPERATION AGREEMENT This Strategic Cooperation Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into as of November 3, 2026 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Alphega Innovations Corporation, a Wyoming corporation (“AIC”), with offices at 30 N Gould St Ste R, Sheridan, WY 82801, and Maison Bouvier Inc., a Colorado corporation (“Party A”), with offices at 1500 N Grant St Ste R, Denver, CO 80203. AIC and Party A are each a “Party” and collectively the “Parties.” RECITALS WHEREAS , the Parties wish to establish a strategic partnership to originate, evaluate, structure and execute corporate, acquisition, financing and other commercial transactions through AIC and, where appropriate, a majority-owned subsidiary; WHEREAS , Party A expects to contribute transaction opportunities, strategic relationships, business development and transaction execution support, and AIC expects to contribute strategic oversight, corporate infrastructure, financial analysis and transaction structuring expertise; WHEREAS , Party A proposes to invest US$400,000 in AIC in exchange for Common Shares pursuant to a separate Investment Rights Agreement; WHEREAS , separately from the Common Shares purchased with such investment, Party A may earn up to 6,000 Series B Preferred Shares through qualifying transaction performance during a three-year earn-out period, subject to the conditions of this Agreement and a separate Share Grant Agreement; and WHEREAS , the Parties contemplate forming Alphega XYZ Corp (“NewCo”), or such other name as the Parties may mutually agree upon, as a management and services platform, subject to appropriate organizational and governance documents. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein, the Parties agree as follows: 1. Purpose of Cooperation The Parties will cooperate to identify, introduce, evaluate and, where approved by AIC, pursue acquisitions, mergers, strategic partnerships, joint ventures, financings, restructurings, investments and other business opportunities. Nothing in this Agreement obligates AIC or its affiliates to pursue or consummate any opportunity. 2. Formation, Ownership and Governance of NewCo 2.1 Formation and Purpose. The Parties intend to form NewCo as a management and services platform supporting AIC’s corporate finance, strategic development and transaction structuring activities. Formation and operations shall be subject to applicable law and definitive organizational documents. 2.2 Ownership. Upon formation and issuance pursuant to definitive documents, NewCo is contemplated to be owned 80% by AIC and 20% by Party A, subject to the NewCo capitalization and governing documents. NewCo equity is distinct from Common Shares and Series B Preferred Shares of AIC. 2.3 Governance. AIC shall exercise strategic oversight. Party A shall have the right to designate one director of NewCo while Party A has completed the US$400,000 Strategic Investment and continues to beneficially own Series B Preferred Shares, subject to applicable law and NewCo governing documents. The bylaws or other governing documents shall address management, distributions, transfers and repurchase rights. Strategic Cooperation Agreement | AIC Inc / Maison Bouvier Inc. 3. Contributions of the Parties 3.1 Party A. Party A shall use commercially reasonable efforts to originate and introduce appropriate transaction opportunities; provide relevant strategic contacts, commercial information and reasonable support for evaluation, negotiation and execution; and cooperate with applicable due diligence and reporting requirements. 3.2 AIC. AIC shall provide strategic oversight, platform resources, transaction evaluation and structuring support, and such personnel and corporate infrastructure as AIC determines appropriate in its business judgment. 4. Strategic Investment and Common Shares 4.1 Commitment. Party A agrees to invest an aggregate of US$400,000 in AIC, or to cause one or more other persons or entities to invest such amount in AIC on its behalf (the “Strategic Investment”), in exchange solely for AIC Common Shares, on the price, issuance, representations and other terms set forth in a separate Investment Rights Agreement. No Common Share quantity or price is established by this Agreement. 4.2 Timing. The Strategic Investment shall be funded within 90 days after execution of this Agreement, and may be funded in multiple tranches, subject to the Investment Rights Agreement. Common Shares shall be issuable only in respect of funds actually received by AIC and upon satisfaction of applicable issuance conditions. 4.3 Separate Consideration. The Strategic Investment and its corresponding Common Shares are separate and independent from the contingent Series B Preferred Share earn-out in Section 5. Payment of the Strategic Investment alone does not earn, vest or entitle Party A to Series B Preferred Shares. No Series B Preferred Shares shall vest unless the full US$400,000 has been received by AIC. 4.4 Funding Default. If Party A fails to complete the Strategic Investment by the applicable deadline, AIC may, upon written notice and subject to any applicable cure provisions in the Investment Rights Agreement, suspend participation or terminate this Agreement. Such termination shall not require issuance of unearned preferred shares. 5. Contingent Performance Earn-Out of Series B Preferred Shares 5.1 Maximum and Period. Subject to this Agreement, the Share Grant Agreement and all required approvals, Party A may earn up to 6,000 AIC Series B Preferred Shares (the “Earn-Out Shares”) solely through achievement of the performance milestones below during the three (3) years following the Effective Date (the “Earn-Out Period”). Unvested Earn-Out Shares expire and are forfeited automatically at the end of the Earn-Out Period. They are not consideration for the Strategic Investment. 5.2 Qualified Transaction. A “Qualified Transaction” means an opportunity first introduced by Party A and successfully completed by AIC, NewCo or a AIC affiliate consisting of: (a) third-party equity or debt capital actually funded, excluding Party A’s initial US$400,000 Strategic Investment; (b) an acquisition, merger, strategic partnership, joint venture, financing, restructuring or other corporate transaction; or (c) an opportunity producing financial consolidation, recurring revenue, transaction fees, strategic assets or other measurable economic benefit. 5.3 Conditions for Credit. A transaction will qualify only if (a) Party A first introduced it to AIC; (b) AIC, NewCo or the applicable affiliate formally accepted it for evaluation or pursuit; (c) it was actually closed, funded or otherwise consummated within the Earn-Out Period; and (d) AIC’s Board determines in good faith that Party A made a significant, substantive contribution to origination, development, negotiation or closing, beyond merely making an initial introduction, and that the transaction produced a material economic benefit. No opportunity previously known to, actively pursued by or previously introduced to AIC, NewCo or their affiliates may be credited. No transaction may be counted twice. Strategic Cooperation Agreement | AIC Inc / Maison Bouvier Inc. 5.4 Qualified Transaction Value. “Qualified Transaction Value” means (a) for financings, gross third-party capital actually funded and received; (b) for acquisitions, mergers and strategic investments, total transaction value stated in definitive closing documents; (c) for joint ventures and strategic partnerships, value reasonably determined by the Board based on economic value attributable to AIC; and (d) for consolidated businesses, fair value determined in good faith by the Board. The Board shall avoid double counting overlapping transactions or economic value. 5.5 Vesting Formula. The Earn-Out Shares shall vest proportionately at the rate of 1,000 Series B Preferred Shares for each US$50,000,000 of aggregate certified Qualified Transaction Value, up to 6,000 shares at US$300,000,000. The corresponding illustrative milestones are US$50 million / 1,000 shares; US$100 million / 2,000; US$150 million / 3,000; US$200 million / 4,000; US$250 million / 5,000; and US$300 million / 6,000. Fractional shares shall not be issued; any fractional entitlement shall be rounded down until additional value is certified. Vesting is subject to Section 5.3 and full funding under Section 4.3. 5.6 Board Certification. No Earn-Out Shares shall be earned or vested until AIC’s Board certifies the applicable Qualified Transaction Value and corresponding number of Earn-Out Shares in good faith. Its determination shall be final absent manifest error, and the Board may consult legal counsel, auditors, valuation professionals or other advisors. Any previously certified value shall be deducted from subsequent cumulative calculations. 5.7 Correction and Clawback. Subject to applicable law and the terms of the issued securities, AIC may correct a certification and seek cancellation, recovery or other lawful remedies if transaction values were materially overstated, introductions were materially misrepresented, or fraud occurred. Any recovery of already issued shares shall be implemented only through legally available procedures. 5.8 Share Rights and Compliance. The original form of Strategic Cooperation Agreement contemplates that each Series B Preferred Share is convertible into 1,000 Common Shares and carries an 8% cumulative preferred dividend. These rights shall apply only if, and to the extent, validly established in AIC’s applicable certificate of designation and definitive Share Grant Agreement. All issuance, vesting, conversion, dividend and retention rights are subject to Board approval, AIC’s charter and bylaws, applicable corporate and securities laws, SEC reporting and accounting requirements, stockholder or exchange approvals where applicable, and directors’ fiduciary duties. Nothing requires an unlawful issuance. 6. Services and Compensation 6.1 Party A may provide origination, financial analysis, business development, structuring, management and transaction execution support. Any management, advisory, service, structuring, success or closing fee shall require a separate written agreement approved by AIC or NewCo, as applicable, and shall be commercially reasonable and compliant with applicable law and related-party policies. 6.2 No fee is promised by this Agreement, and any permitted service or transaction fee is distinct from the Strategic Investment, NewCo ownership and Earn-Out Shares. No Party shall perform activities requiring broker-dealer, placement agent, investment adviser, lending or other licensing unless appropriately registered or exempt and expressly authorized. 6.3 Any dividends or distributions on Party A’s NewCo ownership shall be governed by NewCo’s definitive organizational documents and applicable law. 7. Deal Origination, Acceptance and Allocation AIC and NewCo retain sole discretion to accept, reject, defer, reallocate or discontinue any proposed transaction, taking into account strategic fit, commercial viability, risk, available resources, regulatory considerations and execution feasibility. AIC shall consult Party A in good faith when practicable. Formal acceptance for evaluation does not constitute an obligation to close or a promise of equity vesting. Strategic Cooperation Agreement | AIC Inc / Maison Bouvier Inc. 8. Reporting, Cooperation and Compliance NewCo is expected to prepare monthly financial statements within 15 days of month-end, quarterly reports within 30 days of quarter-end and annual financial statements within 45 days of year-end, subject to its governing documents. Party A shall provide reasonably requested supporting information for transaction diligence, audit, compliance and reporting. Each Party shall comply with applicable law and refrain from representing that it may bind the other without written authorization. 9. Representations and Warranties Each Party represents that it is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction; has requisite power and authority to execute and perform this Agreement; has obtained necessary corporate approvals; and its execution does not violate binding obligations. Party A further represents that it will not knowingly submit materially false transaction information or claim credit for opportunities not originated by it. 10. Termination and Effect 10.1 AIC may terminate this Agreement upon Party A’s material breach remaining uncured for 15 days after written notice, or immediately for fraud, willful misconduct or material reputational harm. Either Party may terminate by mutual written agreement. 10.2 Upon termination, Party A shall cease holding itself out as affiliated with AIC or NewCo. Accrued, properly approved compensation for completed services remains payable. NewCo equity shall be governed by its governing documents. Earn-Out Shares already duly vested and issued remain subject to their governing terms and lawful remedies; unvested Earn-Out Shares cease to be earnable upon termination, unless the Parties expressly agree otherwise in writing. Confidentiality and other provisions intended to survive shall survive. 11. Integrated Agreement Structure This Agreement is intended to operate alongside a separate Investment Rights Agreement, Share Grant Agreement, and NewCo bylaws and/or management agreements. Each instrument governs its specific subject matter. In the event of a conflict, the more specific definitive agreement governs that subject matter, except that no such instrument shall be construed to treat the Earn-Out Shares as consideration for the US$400,000 Strategic Investment absent a written amendment expressly signed by both Parties. 12. Confidentiality Each Party shall protect nonpublic financial, technical, commercial and proprietary information received from the other and use it only to evaluate or perform this Agreement. Disclosure is permitted to personnel, affiliates and professional advisors with a legitimate need to know and equivalent confidentiality obligations, or as required by law with prior notice when lawful. Exclusions include information publicly available without breach, previously lawfully known, or independently developed. Each Party shall exercise reasonable care, no less than it uses for its own confidential information. These obligations survive for three years after termination, or longer as required by law. 13. Governing Law and Jurisdiction This Agreement shall be governed by Wyoming law without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts located in Wyoming for disputes arising under this Agreement. Strategic Cooperation Agreement | AIC Inc / Maison Bouvier Inc. 14. Miscellaneous 14.1 Amendments. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties. 14.2 Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party’s prior written consent, except as expressly permitted in a definitive agreement. 14.3 Relationship. Nothing herein creates a general partnership, agency or fiduciary relationship between the Parties. 14.4 Entire Agreement. This Agreement and the definitive agreements identified in Section 11 constitute the contemplated integrated relationship, subject to their respective terms. 14.5 Counterparts and Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each deemed an original. SIGNATURE PAGE IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Strategic Cooperation Agreement as of the Effective Date. Alphega Innovations Corporation(“AIC”) By: /s/ Luis Carlos Ung Name: Luis Carlos Ung Title: CEO Date: 11/03/2026 Maison Bouvier Inc. (“Party A”) By: /s/ Ihsan Karim Name: Ihsan Karim Title: Owner Date: 11/03/2026 Strategic Cooperation Agreement | AIC Inc / Maison Bouvier Inc.
