text: EX-10.2 3 alpga_ex10-2.htm IP & BUSINESS ASSET ACQUISITION, STRATEGIC COMMERCIALIZATION & SHARE CONSIDERATION AGREEMENT IP and Business Asset Acquisition Strategic Commercialization and Share Consideration Agreement INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND BUSINESS ASSET ACQUISITION, STRATEGIC COMMERCIALIZATION & SHARE CONSIDERATION AGREEMENT ALPHEGA INNOVATIONS CORPORATION | SUMMIT STRATEGIC HOLDINGS CONFIDENTIAL - NOVEMBER 3, 2026 This INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND BUSINESS ASSET ACQUISITION, STRATEGIC COMMERCIALIZATION & SHARE CONSIDERATION AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is entered into as of November 3, 2026 (the “Effective Date”) between Alphega Innovations Corporation, a Wyoming corporation (“AIC” or “Buyer”), and Summit Strategic Holdings, legal entity name, formation jurisdiction and registration number to be confirmed (“SSH” or “Seller”). RECITALS WHEREAS , Summit Strategic Holdings (“SSH”) develops and commercializes intellectual property, proprietary business concepts, technologies, and strategic frameworks in intelligent cities, sustainable communities, advanced technologies, and integrated economic ecosystems, including the Smart City, Terra City, TerraSmart™, and Quinary City™; WHEREAS , these concepts have evolved through the combined efforts of various technology, engineering, urban development, and strategic partners, which SSH has commercialized into a unified, adaptable platform for different SPVs; WHEREAS , through its development and commercialization activities, SSH owns certain proprietary intellectual property, business models, methodologies, commercial frameworks, know-how, and related assets, together with certain contractual and commercialization rights (collectively, the “Underlying Platform”), as identified in Schedule A; and WHEREAS , leveraging the Underlying Platform, SSH has developed a customized integrated IP and business commercialization platform for Alphega Innovations Corporation (“AIC”) known as “Alphega Quinary City™” (the “AIC Platform”), incorporating proprietary business architecture, strategic methodologies, commercialization models, and technology integration frameworks, as described in the Alphega Quinary City SPV Business Plan (the “Business Plan”); WHEREAS , the AIC Platform is intended to provide a scalable and replicable framework for the development, promotion, implementation, management, and long-term operation of intelligent and sustainable communities, integrating artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, advanced technologies, sustainable development solutions, innovation ecosystems, and lifecycle services; WHEREAS , SSH desires to sell, assign, and transfer to AIC, and AIC desires to purchase and acquire, the specified intellectual property, proprietary business assets, and transferable commercialization rights comprising the AIC Platform, enabling AIC, directly or through its subsidiaries or special-purpose vehicles, to further develop, customize, promote, market, license, and commercialize the platform under the Alphega Quinary City™ and Terra City brands, and such other branding as AIC may adopt, subject to applicable third-party intellectual property and trademark rights; WHEREAS , AIC recognizes the strategic and commercial potential of the AIC Platform and intends to utilize the acquired intellectual property, business assets, and commercialization rights to establish and expand its business activities in intelligent infrastructure, sustainable communities, technology integration, development management, and related commercial services; NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the foregoing premises, the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, the issuance of AIC common shares as provided in this Agreement, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereby agree as follows: 1. DEFINITIONS “ AIC Platform ” means the customized and integrated intellectual property and business commercialization platform developed by SSH for AIC under the name “Alphega Quinary City™,” including the Business Plan and the Acquired Assets identified in Schedule A, intended for further development, promotion, licensing, and commercialization by AIC. “Acquired Intellectual Property and Business Assets” or “Acquired Assets” means the intellectual property, proprietary business assets, original works, business concepts, commercial architectures, methodologies, operating frameworks, models, plans, documented know-how, and related rights expressly identified in Schedule A as either (i) “SSH-Owned - Assigned,” being assets owned by SSH and assigned to AIC, or (ii) “Mandated Rights - Authorized Transfer or License,” being rights of participating owners that SSH is authorized to arrange for assignment or licensing to AIC under the applicable written instruments. Mandated assets are transferred only to the extent authorized by their respective rights holders. Excluded or reference materials are not Acquired Assets. “ Closing Package ” means the documents, assets, instruments, and supporting evidence specified in Schedule C. “ Excluded Third-Party IP ” means intellectual property independently owned by technology providers, engineering participants, development partners, or other third parties that is not expressly assigned or licensed to AIC under the applicable written agreements. “Licensed Rights” means intellectual property, technology, trademarks, know-how, or other commercial rights expressly licensed or sublicensed to AIC pursuant to this Agreement or a separate written instrument identified in Schedule A, including rights arranged by SSH under a participating owner’s mandate where duly authorized. “ Milestone Deliverables ” means the post-Closing deliverables specified in Schedule B. “ Underlying Platform ” means the integrated business, technology, development, and commercialization framework associated with the Smart City, Terra City, TerraSmart™, and Quinary City™ initiatives, comprising proprietary elements developed or owned by SSH together with complementary concepts, technologies, and resources contributed by or associated with independent third parties. 2. PURCHASE AND SALE OF INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND BUSINESS ASSETS 2.1 Purchase and Assignment. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, at Closing, SSH hereby sells, assigns, transfers, and conveys to AIC all of SSH’s right, title, and interest in the assets identified in Schedule A as “SSH-Owned - Assigned,” including associated transferable intellectual property rights. For assets identified as “Mandated Rights - Authorized Transfer or License,” SSH shall arrange the assignment or licensing of the applicable rights through duly authorized instruments executed by the relevant rights holders or otherwise legally effective authorizations. No independently owned third-party asset shall be deemed assigned by SSH solely by virtue of its commercialization mandate. Assigned rights shall be worldwide, perpetual, and exclusive only to the extent specified in the applicable assignment instruments, subject to disclosed restrictions and encumbrances. 2.2 Delivery and Documentation. SSH shall deliver to AIC the Acquired Assets in reasonably complete electronic and editable formats, including available supporting documentation, technical and commercial materials, business models, operating frameworks, and related records. SSH shall execute such additional assignments, confirmations, and other instruments as may reasonably be necessary to evidence, perfect, or give effect to the transfer of the Acquired Assets. 2.3 Commercialization and Branding Rights. AIC shall have the perpetual and worldwide right to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, enhance, integrate, develop, market, promote, distribute, license, sublicense, and otherwise commercialize the Assigned Acquired Assets, directly or through its subsidiaries, affiliates, special-purpose vehicles, and authorized commercial partners, without further consent from or additional compensation to SSH, except as expressly provided in this Agreement. Such rights include the ability to develop and commercialize the AIC Platform under the Alphega Quinary City™ and Terra City™ brands and other branding adopted by AIC, provided that use of any independently owned third-party trademarks or intellectual property shall be subject to the applicable licenses or authorizations. 2.4 Licensed and Third-Party Rights. To the extent that any component of the Underlying Platform is owned by a third party or is otherwise not legally assignable by SSH, such component shall not be deemed transferred by this Agreement unless the applicable rights holder has executed an appropriate assignment or other legally effective authorization. Any Licensed Rights included in the transaction shall be expressly identified in Schedule A and supported by written licenses, sublicenses, or other applicable instruments specifying their scope, duration, permitted uses, and transferability. 2.5 Independent Commercialization Authority and Post-Closing Relationship. SSH shall maintain the authority necessary to arrange the transfer or licensing of the applicable rights identified in Schedule A. SSH’s underlying mandates, business relationships, and third-party arrangements shall remain independent of AIC and shall not form part of this Agreement. Following Closing, AIC shall independently own and commercialize the acquired rights, and SSH shall have no continuing operational, management, or commercialization obligations except as expressly provided herein or mutually agreed in writing. 2.6 Retained Rights. Except for rights expressly transferred or licensed under this Agreement, SSH and the applicable third-party rights holders shall retain their respective intellectual property and other proprietary rights. Nothing herein shall be construed as transferring ownership of independently owned technologies, land, physical developments, government approvals, project contracts, or other assets not specifically identified in Schedule A. 3. AUTHORITY, TITLE AND THIRD-PARTY RIGHTS 3.1 Ownership and Mandated Authority. SSH represents and warrants that it owns certain Acquired Assets and holds commercialization mandates for others identified in Schedule A. SSH may assign its owned assets and arrange the transfer or licensing of mandated assets to AIC, subject to applicable authorizations and required consents. 3.2 Collaborative Development and Third-Party Contributions. The Underlying Platform incorporates contributions of independent parties. SSH may contribute its owned proprietary assets and coordinate the transfer or licensing of additional rights within the scope of its written mandates. No third-party ownership interest passes to AIC without a legally effective assignment, license, or other written rights-holder authorization. 3.3 Intellectual Property Documentation. SSH shall provide a reasonably complete Schedule A identifying each asset or right, the owner, SSH’s ownership or mandate basis, proposed assignment or license treatment, material restrictions, and required consents. Available ownership records, assignments, licenses, and authorizations shall support the applicable Closing transfers. SSH shall retain its underlying third-party mandates separately. 3.4 No Conflicting Rights . SSH represents and warrants, to its knowledge after reasonable inquiry and except as disclosed in Schedule A, that transfers of SSH-owned assets and the mandated arrangements SSH undertakes within their authorized scope will not violate binding agreements or known third-party rights. SSH does not warrant title to independently owned third-party assets. 3.5 Further Assurances. SSH shall reasonably cooperate with AIC following Closing in executing additional documents, confirming ownership or authorization, and completing such other formalities as may reasonably be necessary to give effect to the transfer of the Acquired Assets and Licensed Rights contemplated by this Agreement. 4. BUSINESS SCOPE AND COMMERCIAL PURPOSE The AIC Platform constitutes an integrated intellectual property and business commercialization framework intended to support the development, promotion, implementation, management, and long-term operation of intelligent, sustainable communities and interconnected economic ecosystems. The platform incorporates proprietary business methodologies, development and commercialization strategies, technology integration frameworks, operating models, and related business assets, together with authorized applications of complementary technologies and development concepts. Its contemplated commercial activities include strategic feasibility and master planning, project origination, development and program management, artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure integration, sustainable infrastructure solutions, innovation and enterprise development, systems integration, maintenance, lifecycle operations, and replication across multiple geographic markets. AIC may pursue these activities directly or through designated subsidiaries, special-purpose vehicles, joint ventures, licensing arrangements, and other commercial structures, subject to applicable laws, corporate approvals, and third-party contractual rights. The Parties acknowledge that the AIC Platform is intended to function as a scalable and adaptable business and services platform and does not, by itself, constitute ownership of any particular city, development site, physical infrastructure, government concession, or independently owned third-party technology. 5. CLOSING; INITIAL CONSIDERATION 5.1 Purchase Consideration Subject to satisfaction of the Closing conditions set forth in Section 5.2, AIC shall issue 1,500,000 shares of its common stock (the “Initial Shares”) to SSH as consideration for the acquisition of the intellectual property, proprietary business assets, and associated commercialization rights identified in Schedule A. The Initial Shares shall be issued upon completion of the Closing requirements and delivery of the applicable transfer documentation, subject to the corporate and securities-law requirements set forth in this Agreement. 5.2 Closing conditions The Parties intend to complete Closing promptly, subject to the following conditions: (a) Both Parties execute this Agreement and substantially finalized Schedule A, with Schedules B–C completed or supplemented as mutually agreed; (b) SSH delivers the principal Acquired Assets and reasonably sufficient documentation evidencing its ownership or authority to transfer the rights included at Closing. Supplementary documentation, confirmations, and nonessential third-party authorizations may be delivered after Closing as mutually agreed; (c) AIC obtains the necessary corporate authorization and confirms the availability of shares for issuance; (d) The issuance of shares complies with applicable securities laws, including an effective registration statement or available exemption, and SSH provides required investor representations; and (e) Any outstanding administrative matters, supplemental documentation, or nonmaterial deliverables may be completed after Closing within mutually agreed periods. The Parties may waive or defer nonessential conditions by mutual written agreement, provided that no waiver shall eliminate any mandatory legal requirement or authorize the transfer of rights without the necessary legal authority. 5.3 Nature of Consideration and Accounting The Initial Shares constitute consideration for the acquisition of the intellectual property, proprietary business assets, and associated commercialization rights identified in Schedule A. The Initial Shares are not consideration for SSH’s separate third-party mandates or for speculative future project awards, financing transactions, or commercial returns. AIC shall evaluate and account for the transaction in accordance with applicable U.S. GAAP, based on the substance of the acquired assets, their supported fair value, and the relevant contractual arrangements. 6. ADDITIONAL MILESTONE SHARES 6.1 Additional Milestone Consideration In addition to the Initial Shares, AIC shall issue up to 1,000,000 additional shares of AIC common stock to SSH upon satisfactory completion and written acceptance of the distinct Milestone Deliverables specified in Schedule B, subject to applicable corporate approvals and securities-law requirements. The Milestone Shares shall be allocated as follows: (a) 400,000 shares upon completion and delivery of the Integrated Technology and Intellectual Property Framework Package; (b) 300,000 shares upon completion and delivery of the SPV Business and Commercialization Framework Package; and (c) 300,000 shares upon completion and delivery of the Commercial Launch and Platform Handover Package. Each milestone shall be evaluated independently based on the deliverables and acceptance criteria set forth in Schedule B. The applicable Milestone Shares shall be issued within thirty (30) days following written acceptance of the corresponding Milestone Deliverables, subject to satisfaction of applicable corporate and securities-law requirements. 6.2 Milestone Deliverables The Milestone Deliverables shall be separate from the Acquired Assets delivered at Closing and shall be completed and accepted in accordance with Schedule B and Section 7. Any material modification to the scope of the Milestone Deliverables shall require the written agreement of both Parties. 6.3 Additional Transactions Additional business plans, independently valuable IP, projects, commercial contracts, acquisitions or strategic opportunities introduced by SSH may support further equity or other consideration only under a separate, AIC-board-approved written agreement identifying actual consideration, valuation, approvals and securities-law treatment. No automatic entitlement, minimum or unlimited preauthorization is created. 7. DELIVERY, REVIEW AND ACCEPTANCE SSH shall deliver the applicable Milestone Deliverables identified in Schedule B in electronic format, together with the relevant supporting materials reasonably necessary for AIC to review and confirm completion. AIC shall have fifteen (15) business days following receipt to accept the applicable Milestone Deliverables in writing or provide a written notice identifying any material deficiencies. SSH shall have twenty (20) business days to address such deficiencies, and AIC shall have ten (10) business days to review the resubmitted materials. Acceptance shall not be unreasonably withheld where the applicable acceptance criteria have been satisfied. Any disagreement concerning acceptance shall first be referred to the Parties’ authorized representatives for resolution. To the extent any Milestone Deliverables include intellectual property or proprietary business materials developed specifically for AIC, SSH shall assign the applicable transferable rights to AIC upon written acceptance of the relevant Milestone Deliverables, and the corresponding Milestone Shares shall be issued in accordance with Section 6, subject to applicable corporate and securities-law requirements. 8. COMMERCIALIZATION AND CORPORATE CONTROL 8.1 Commercialization Rights AIC shall have the right to develop, promote, market, license, and commercialize the AIC Platform and the Assigned Acquired Assets directly or through its subsidiaries, special-purpose vehicles, joint ventures, and authorized commercial partners, subject to applicable laws and third-party rights. 8.2 Branding and Market Development AIC may commercialize the AIC Platform under the Alphega Quinary City™ and Terra City brands, together with other branding adopted by AIC, to the extent the applicable trademark and branding rights are owned by AIC, assigned under this Agreement, or otherwise properly licensed or authorized. 8.3 SPV Structure AIC may establish an AIC-controlled special-purpose vehicle or other subsidiary to undertake business development, project origination, technology integration, implementation coordination, licensing, and lifecycle operations associated with the AIC Platform, subject to AIC’s applicable corporate approval procedures. 8.4 Corporate Authority AIC shall retain authority over the governance, capitalization, financing, strategic direction, commercial agreements, and operations of its subsidiaries and special-purpose vehicles. SSH shall have no authority to bind AIC, issue AIC securities, dispose of AIC assets, or independently establish transaction economics on behalf of AIC without express written authorization. 8.5 Additional Commercial Arrangements Any royalties, revenue-sharing arrangements, project participation rights, management fees, or other compensation not expressly provided under this Agreement shall require a separate written agreement duly authorized by AIC. Nothing herein shall modify the rights or obligations of independent third parties under separate agreements to which AIC is not a party. 9. REPRESENTATIONS AND RISK ALLOCATION 9.1 Intellectual Property Representations SSH represents and warrants that: (a) Ownership and Mandated Authority. SSH represents and warrants that it owns certain Acquired Assets and holds commercialization mandates for others identified in Schedule A. SSH may assign its owned assets and arrange the transfer or licensing of mandated assets to AIC, subject to applicable authorizations and required consents; (b) To SSH’s knowledge after reasonable inquiry, the assignment and intended use of the Acquired Assets as expressly contemplated by this Agreement will not infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights of any third party; (c) SSH has disclosed in Schedule A all material ownership restrictions, existing licenses, competing rights, and third-party consents known to SSH that may materially affect AIC’s intended use of the Acquired Assets; and (d) SSH has not knowingly granted any rights that would materially impair the ownership or commercialization rights expressly conveyed to AIC under this Agreement. 9.2 Commercial Limitations SSH does not guarantee that the AIC Platform will result in completed development projects, government approvals, financing commitments, commercial contracts, particular revenue levels, profitability, or specified investment returns. Illustrative financial projections and development scenarios contained in the Business Plan or supporting materials are not contractual warranties. 9.3 Regulatory Requirements Any activities involving engineering, architecture, construction, regulated utilities, digital assets, securities, tokenization, artificial intelligence, personal data, or other regulated services shall be undertaken only in accordance with applicable laws, approvals, and professional requirements. 10. SECURITIES; ACCOUNTING; DISCLOSURE Shares shall be issued only under valid corporate authorization and an effective registration statement or available exemption; absent lawful free tradability, they shall be restricted securities with appropriate legends and transfer-agent controls. SSH shall deliver subscription/investment representations and beneficial ownership information reasonably required. AIC shall determine required SEC disclosures, related-party analysis if relevant, fair-value support and accounting recognition in consultation with its counsel and auditors. AIC and SSH shall reasonably cooperate in providing documentation necessary to support the accounting, valuation, corporate authorization, and disclosure requirements applicable to the transaction, including information concerning the nature, ownership, transferability, and commercial application of the Acquired Assets. Neither Party shall be required to adopt an accounting classification or valuation that is inconsistent with applicable accounting standards or the underlying economic substance of the transaction. 11. CONFIDENTIALITY AND PUBLIC STATEMENTS Each Party shall protect nonpublic information using reasonable care and disclose it only to authorized recipients under confidentiality obligations, subject to legal disclosures. Neither Party may announce a completed transfer of third-party IP or use another owner’s marks without authority. AIC may make legally required public-company disclosures. Following Closing, AIC may publicly describe its acquisition, ownership, development, and commercialization of the AIC Platform and the Acquired Assets, subject to applicable securities laws, confidentiality obligations, and third-party intellectual property rights. SSH shall not make public statements purporting to bind AIC or announcing transactions, financing commitments, or project awards on behalf of AIC without AIC’s prior written authorization, except as required by law. 12. TERM; TERMINATION; SURVIVAL 12.1 Continuing Effect. The acquisition and assignment of the Acquired Assets shall become effective upon Closing and shall remain in effect in accordance with the terms of this Agreement. 12.2 Milestone Deliverables. The Milestone Deliverables shall be completed and accepted in accordance with Sections 6 and 7 and Schedule B. Either Party may terminate the affected outstanding Milestone Deliverables upon a material breach by the other Party that remains uncured for thirty (30) days following written notice specifying the breach. Such termination shall not affect any Milestone Deliverables previously completed and accepted. 12.3 Effect of Termination. Termination of any outstanding Milestone Deliverables shall not affect AIC’s ownership of Acquired Assets validly transferred under this Agreement or any Milestone Shares previously earned and validly issued. Milestone Shares attributable to any terminated and uncompleted Milestone Deliverables shall not become payable, unless otherwise agreed in writing. 12.4 Survival. The provisions concerning intellectual property ownership, representations and warranties, confidentiality, indemnification, and dispute resolution shall survive Closing or termination to the extent applicable. Licensed Rights shall remain subject to their respective license agreements. 13. INDEMNITY AND LIMITATIONS Each Party shall indemnify the other against third-party claims to the extent caused by its material breach, fraud, willful misconduct, unauthorized commitments or infringement by materials it supplied, excluding losses caused by the indemnitee. Neither Party guarantees commercial success. Except for fraud, willful misconduct, IP misappropriation, confidentiality breaches and non-excludable liability, neither Party shall be liable for speculative lost profits or indirect consequential damages. No monetary liability cap is agreed. SSH shall indemnify AIC against losses, damages, liabilities, and reasonable legal expenses arising from third-party claims resulting from SSH’s material breach of its representations concerning ownership, authority to transfer, or infringement of intellectual property rights in the Assigned Acquired Assets, subject to the limitations and exclusions expressly provided in this Agreement. 14. GENERAL 14.1 Independent Parties. The Parties are independent contracting parties. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture, agency, fiduciary relationship, or employment relationship between the Parties. 14.2 Amendments. Any amendment, modification, or supplement to this Agreement shall be effective only if made in writing and executed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties. Any additional issuance of AIC securities shall remain subject to applicable corporate approvals and securities laws. 14.3 Assignment and Transfer. Neither Party may assign its obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party, except as otherwise expressly provided herein. AIC may assign, transfer, license, sublicense, or otherwise commercialize the Acquired Assets and associated rights, directly or through its subsidiaries, affiliates, special-purpose vehicles, or successors, subject to applicable restrictions on Licensed Rights. Any assignment of contractual obligations shall not release the assigning Party from its obligations unless otherwise agreed in writing. 14.4 Notices. All notices required or permitted under this Agreement shall be made in writing and delivered to the respective addresses or email contacts designated by the Parties in the execution section, or to such other contact information as either Party may subsequently designate by written notice. 14.5 Counterparts and Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one agreement. Electronic signatures shall have the same legal effect as original signatures to the extent permitted by applicable law. 14.6 Governing Law and Jurisdiction. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Wyoming, without regard to its conflict-of-law principles. The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Wyoming for any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement. 14.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with its executed schedules and any documents expressly incorporated herein, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties concerning the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior discussions, negotiations, and understandings between them relating to such subject matter. Nothing herein shall modify or supersede the rights or obligations of third parties under separate agreements to which AIC is not a party. 14.8 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect, provided that the essential commercial purpose of this Agreement is not materially affected. 14.9 Further Assurances. Each Party shall execute and deliver such additional documents and take such reasonable actions as may be necessary to give effect to the transactions expressly contemplated by this Agreement. SCHEDULE A - ACQUIRED INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY, BUSINESS ASSETS AND COMMERCIALIZATION RIGHTS Schedule A distinguishes (i) SSH-owned assets assigned directly to AIC; (ii) rights held by participating owners that SSH is mandated to commercialize and may arrange to transfer or license only with the required written authorizations; and (iii) excluded or reference-only third-party materials. The applicable ownership, consent, and transfer documentation shall be identified in the Closing Package; SSH shall retain any underlying mandates separately. A commercialization mandate alone does not convey title to independently owned third-party intellectual property. Asset Category Rights Classification / Treatment Alphega Quinary City SPV Business Plan and original SSH-owned content SSH-Owned - Assigned SSH-owned commercialization frameworks and methodologies SSH-Owned - Assigned SSH-owned business models, operating architecture and replication methodologies SSH-Owned - Assigned SSH-owned strategic planning, project qualification and development management materials SSH-Owned - Assigned SSH-owned financial and commercial models, templates and supporting documentation SSH-Owned - Assigned SSH-owned improvements and derivative works SSH-Owned - Assigned Terra City branding SSH-Owned - Assigned, subject to title verification Quinary City™ / TerraSmart™ branding Mandated Rights - Licensed only with rights-holder authorization Third-party engineering and technology IP Third-Party IP - Excluded or separately licensed Existing regional project concepts and references Reference materials only - No transfer Additional third-party concepts, methodologies or project-related rights specifically listed in an executed rights-holder instrument Mandated Rights - Authorized Transfer or License; rights-holder instrument required SCHEDULE B - POST-CLOSING DELIVERABLES AND MILESTONES Milestone 1 - Integrated Technology and Intellectual Property Framework Package Share Consideration: 400,000 AIC Common Shares Completion and delivery of an AIC-specific integrated framework package organizing and adapting the acquired business architecture, technology integration concepts, intellectual property framework, and commercialization methodologies into a consolidated reference package for AIC’s intended commercial applications, together with supplementary explanatory materials and updated framework documentation developed following Closing. Acceptance Criteria: Delivery of the completed framework documentation and supporting materials in electronic format, reasonably consistent with the Business Plan and the Acquired Assets identified in Schedule A. _______________________________________________________________________ Milestone 2 - SPV Business and Commercialization Framework Package Share Consideration: 300,000 AIC Common Shares Completion and delivery of an AIC-specific business and commercialization framework covering the proposed SPV structure, business model, principal service lines, strategic development approach, commercial applications, and potential partnership arrangements associated with the AIC Platform. Acceptance Criteria: Delivery of the completed business and commercialization framework, including the proposed SPV operating concept and commercialization roadmap, in electronic format. _______________________________________________________________________ Milestone 3 - Commercial Launch and Platform Handover Package Share Consideration: 300,000 AIC Common Shares Completion and delivery of the AIC-branded commercialization package, including consolidated business presentation materials, platform positioning, proposed commercial applications, market-development materials, and final organization and handover of the relevant platform documentation. Acceptance Criteria: Delivery of the completed commercialization materials and organized platform documentation in electronic format, suitable for AIC’s subsequent adaptation and commercial use, subject to applicable intellectual property and branding rights. _______________________________________________________________________ General Provisions Each milestone shall be considered completed upon delivery and written acceptance of the applicable documentation package in accordance with Section 7 of the Agreement. The Milestone Deliverables shall be distinct from the assets delivered at Closing and shall be evaluated based on the applicable documentation and materials specified above. Any changes to the scope of the Milestone Deliverables shall be mutually agreed upon in writing by the Parties. SCHEDULE C - CLOSING PACKAGE AND EVIDENCE 1. Executed Agreement and finalized signed asset inventory (Schedule A). 2. Final identified October 2026 Business Plan and native/editable files, including annexes and original materials being sold. 3. Evidence reasonably sufficient to establish SSH’s authority to arrange the applicable rights, together with executed rights-holder consents or transfer/license instruments required for assets included at Closing. SSH’s underlying mandates remain separate and are not incorporated into this Agreement. 6. AIC board authorization and share availability confirmation. 7. Securities exemption and investor representation documentation. 8. Fair-value/accounting support and transfer-agent issuance instructions. 9. Completed notice contacts, effective date, and other applicable execution details. SCHEDULE D - BUSINESS PLAN / TECHNOLOGY FRAMEWORK REFERENCE The acquired Business Plan describes a site-neutral, exportable development and services business with stages: origination and feasibility; concept and master planning; engineering/design coordination; implementation and systems integration; commissioning; maintenance and operations; expansion and global replication. Technology concepts include AI-native services, GIS/BIM/digital twins, IoT and LoRaWAN connectivity, smart mobility and utilities, renewable energy, sustainable construction, smart hospitality, enterprise incubation and optional regulated digital participation. These are proposed capabilities and commercial frameworks, not representations that AIC acquires independently owned underlying technology or operating project assets. The AIC Platform represents an integrated commercialization framework incorporating proprietary business architecture, development and operating methodologies, and related intellectual property acquired from SSH, together with authorized applications of complementary technologies and services. AIC may further develop, adapt, promote, and commercialize the acquired platform under the branding and rights arrangements expressly established under this Agreement. References to third-party technologies, development initiatives, or project concepts shall not independently constitute an assignment of ownership or a guarantee of commercial implementation.

title: Starlink AI Acquisition Corp
text: EX-10.1 3 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 COMPANY SHAREHOLDERS SUPPORT AGREEMENT This Company Shareholders Support Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is made and entered into as of October 30, 2026, by and among (i) Spider Digital Technology Group, an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands (“ PubCo ”), (ii) Spider Digital Technology Ltd., an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands (the “ Company ”), (iii) certain shareholders of the Company (each, a “ Requisite Shareholder ”), and (iv) Starlink AI Acquisition Corporation, an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands (the “ Acquiror ”). PubCo, the Company, Acquiror, and the Requisite Shareholders are sometimes referred to herein as a “ Party ” and collectively as the “ Parties ”. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the respective meanings ascribed to such terms in the Business Combination Agreement (as defined below). RECITALS A. On October 30, 2026, Acquiror, PubCo, Spider Digital Merger Ltd, an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands and a direct wholly owned Subsidiary of PubCo (“ Merger Sub I ”), StarLink AI Merger Ltd an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands and a direct wholly owned Subsidiary of PubCo (“ Merger Sub II ”), and the Company, entered into a Business Combination Agreement (the “ Business Combination Agreement ”) pursuant to which, upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein: (a) Merger Sub I will merge with and into the Company (the “ First Merger ”), with the Company surviving the First Merger as a wholly-owned subsidiary of PubCo and the outstanding shares of the Company being converted into the right to receive shares of PubCo, and (b) one (1) Business Day following, and as part of the same overall transaction as, the First Merger, Merger Sub II will merge with and into Acquiror (the “ Second Merger ”, and together with the First Merger, the “ Mergers ”), with Acquiror surviving the Second Merger as a wholly-owned subsidiary of PubCo and the outstanding securities of Acquiror being converted into the right to receive shares of PubCo (the Mergers together with the other transactions contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement, the “ Transactions ”). B. Each Requisite Shareholder agrees to enter into this Agreement with respect to all Company Ordinary Shares (the “ Company Shares ”), of which such Requisite Shareholder now or hereafter has beneficial ownership (as such term is defined in Rule 13d-3 under the Exchange Act) and/or record ownership. C. As of the date hereof, each Requisite Shareholder is the owner of, and/or has voting power (including, without limitation, by proxy or power of attorney) over, such number and class of Company Shares as are indicated opposite the name of such Requisite Shareholder on Schedule A attached hereto (all such Company Shares, together with any shares in the Company of which beneficial and/or record ownership and/or the power to vote (including, without limitation, by proxy or power of attorney) is hereafter acquired by any such Requisite Shareholder (or any securities convertible into or exercisable or exchangeable for Company Shares) during the period from the date hereof through the Expiration Time are collectively referred to herein as the “ Subject Shares ”). D. As a condition to the willingness of Acquiror and Company to enter into the Business Combination Agreement and as an inducement and in consideration therefor, the Requisite Shareholders have agreed to enter into this Agreement. E. Each of the Parties has determined that it is in its best interest to enter into this Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing and the respective representations, warranties, covenants and agreements set forth below and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereto, intending to be legally bound, do hereby agree as follows: 1. Definitions . When used in this Agreement, the following terms in all of their tenses, cases and correlative forms shall have the meanings assigned to them in this Section 1 or elsewhere in this Agreement. “ Expiration Time ” shall mean the earliest to occur of (a) the First Merger Effective Time, (b) such date and time as the Business Combination Agreement shall be terminated in accordance with Section 11.1 thereof and (c) this agreement is terminated pursuant to the mutual written agreement of Acquiror, the Company and such Requisite Shareholder. “ Transfer ” shall mean any sale, assignment, encumbrance, pledge, hypothecation, disposition, loan or other transfer, or entry into any contract, agreement, option or other arrangement or understanding with respect to any sale, assignment, encumbrance, pledge, hypothecation, disposition, loan or other transfer, in each case directly or indirectly and voluntarily or involuntarily, of any interest owned by a person or any interest (including a beneficial interest) in, or the ownership, control or possession of, any interest owned by a person, excluding entry into this Agreement and the Business Combination Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby. 2. Agreement to Retain the Subject Shares . 2.1 No Transfer of Subject Shares . Until the Expiration Time, each Requisite Shareholder agrees not to (x) Transfer any Subject Shares or (y) deposit any Subject Shares into a voting trust or enter into a voting agreement with respect to any Subject Shares or grant any proxy (except as otherwise provided herein), consent or power of attorney with respect thereto (other than pursuant to this Agreement). Notwithstanding the foregoing, (A) if a Requisite Shareholder is an individual, such Requisite Shareholder may Transfer any such Subject Shares (i) to any member of such Requisite Shareholder’s immediate family, or to a trust for the benefit of such Requisite Shareholder or any member of such Requisite Shareholder’s immediate family, the sole trustees of which are such Requisite Shareholder or any member of such Requisite Shareholder’s immediate family, (ii) by will, other testamentary document or under the laws of intestacy upon the death of such Requisite Shareholder, (iii) pursuant to a qualified domestic relations order or (iv) pursuant to a charitable gift or contribution, (B) if a Requisite Shareholder is an entity, such Requisite Shareholder may Transfer any Subject Shares to any partner, member, shareholder, or affiliate of such Requisite Shareholder in accordance with the terms of the Governing Documents of the Company, and (C) a Requisite Shareholder may Transfer any Subject Shares upon the consent of Acquiror; provided , that in each case such transferee of such Subject Shares evidences in a writing, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Pubco, Acquiror and the Company, such transferee’s agreement to be bound by and subject to all of the terms and provisions hereof to the same effect as such transferring Requisite Shareholder, prior and as a condition to the occurrence of such Transfer . 2.2 Additional Purchases . Until the Expiration Time, each Requisite Shareholder agrees that any Subject Shares that such Requisite Shareholder purchases, that are issued to such Requisite Shareholder by the Company, that are otherwise hereinafter acquired by such Requisite Shareholder or with respect to which such Requisite Shareholder otherwise acquires sole or shared voting power (including by proxy or power of attorney) after the execution of this Agreement and prior to the Expiration Time, shall in each case be subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement to the same extent as if they were Subject Shares owned by such Requisite Shareholder as of the date hereof. Each of the Requisite Shareholders agrees, while this Agreement is in effect, to notify Pubco, Acquiror and the Company promptly in writing (including by e-mail) of the number of any additional Subject Shares acquired, or over which voting power is acquired, by such Requisite Shareholder, if any, after the date hereof. 2.3 Unpermitted Transfers . Any Transfer or attempted Transfer of any Subject Shares in violation of this Section 2 shall, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable Law, be null and void ab initio . 3. Voting of Subject Shares . Hereafter until the Expiration Time, each Requisite Shareholder hereby unconditionally and irrevocably agrees that, at any meeting of the shareholders of the Company (or any adjournment or postponement thereof), and in any action by written consent of the shareholders of the Company requested by the Governing Documents of the Company or otherwise undertaken as contemplated by the Transactions (which written consent shall be delivered promptly, and in any event not later than two (2) Business Days, after the Company requests such delivery), such Requisite Shareholder shall: if a meeting is held, attend and appear at the meeting, in person or by proxy, or otherwise cause its Subject Shares to be counted as present thereat for purposes of establishing a quorum, and such Requisite Shareholder shall vote all of the Subject Shares to which such Requisite Shareholder has sole or shared voting power and is entitled to vote; and/or if a written consent or approval is requested, duly and promptly execute and provide such written consent or approval (or cause to be voted or so consented or approved), in person or by proxy, in respect of all of its Subject Shares: (i) in favor of (a) the First Merger, the Business Combination Agreement, the Transaction Documents, any required amendments to the Company’s Governing Documents, and all of the other Transactions (and any actions required in furtherance thereof), and (b) the other matters set forth in the Business Combination Agreement (clauses (a) and (b) collectively, the “ Company Shareholder Approval Matters ”), or if there are insufficient votes in favor of granting the approval of the Company Shareholder Approval Matters, in favor of the adjournment or postponement of such meeting of the shareholders of the Company to a later date, (ii) in opposition to, other than as contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement, (x) any material change in the present capitalization of the Company or any amendment of the Company’s Governing Documents, (y) any material change in the Company’s corporate structure or business or (z) any proposal, offer, or submission with respect to an Acquisition Proposal or Alternative Transaction (“ Competing Transaction ”) or the adoption of any agreement to enter into a Competing Transaction; and (iii) in any other circumstances upon which a vote, consent or other approval with respect to the Company Shareholder Approval Matters is sought, to vote, consent or approve (or cause to be voted, consented or approved) all of such Requisite Shareholder’s Subject Shares held at such time in favor of the foregoing; provided , however , that such Requisite Shareholder shall not be required to vote or provide consent or take any other action, in each case to the extent any such vote, consent or other action would preclude SEC registration of the Pubco Ordinary Shares being issued to holders of Company Shares as contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement. 4. Additional Agreements . 4.1 No Challenges . Each Requisite Shareholder agrees not to commence, join in, facilitate, assist or encourage, and agrees to take all actions necessary to opt out of any class in any class action with respect to, any claim, derivative or otherwise, against Acquiror, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II, Pubco, the Company or any of their respective successors or directors (a) challenging the validity of, or seeking to enjoin the operation of, any provision of this Agreement or (b) alleging a breach of any fiduciary duty of any person in connection with the evaluation, negotiation or entry into the Business Combination Agreement or any other agreement in connection with the Transactions. 4.2 Further Actions . Each Requisite Shareholder agrees, while this Agreement is in effect, not to take or omit to take, or agree to commit to take or omit to take, any action that would make any representation and warranty of such Requisite Shareholder contained in this Agreement inaccurate in any material respect. Each Requisite Shareholder further agrees that it shall use its reasonable best efforts to cooperate with Acquiror and the Company to effect the transactions contemplated hereby and the Transactions, including to take or omit to take such actions, and execute such agreements, as may be reasonably requested by Acquiror or the Company in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby and the Transactions or that are necessary to give further effect thereto. 4.3 Consent to Disclosure . Each Requisite Shareholder hereby consents to the publication and disclosure in the Proxy/Registration Statement (and, as and to the extent otherwise required by applicable securities Laws or the SEC or any other securities authorities, any other documents or communications provided by Acquiror, Pubco or the Company to any Governmental Authority or to securityholders of Acquiror) of such Requisite Shareholder’s identity and beneficial ownership of the Subject Shares and the nature of such Requisite Shareholder’s commitments, arrangements and understandings under and relating to this Agreement and, if deemed appropriate by Acquiror, Pubco or the Company, a copy of this Agreement. Each Requisite Shareholder will promptly provide any information reasonably requested by Acquiror, Pubco or the Company for any regulatory application or filing made or approval sought in connection with the Transactions (including filings with the SEC). 4.4 Waiver of Dissenters’ Rights . Each Requisite Shareholder hereby irrevocably waives, and agrees not to exercise or assert, any dissenters’ rights under Section 238 of the Companies Act (as Revised) of the Cayman Islands and any other similar statute in connection with the Transactions and the Business Combination Agreement. 4.5 No Redemption . Each of the Requisite Shareholders undertakes that, from the date hereof and until the termination of this Agreement, it will not elect to cause the Company to redeem any Subject Shares now or at any time legally or beneficially owned by such Requisite Shareholder (whether pursuant to the Governing Documents of the Company, Law, contract or otherwise, notwithstanding such Requisite Shareholder may have rights thereunder), or submit or surrender any of its Subject Shares for redemption. 4.6 New Shares . In the event that prior to the Expiration Time (i) any equity securities of the Company are issued or otherwise distributed to a Requisite Shareholder pursuant to any share dividend or distribution, or any change in any of the Subject Shares or other share capital the Company by reason of any share subdivision, recapitalization, consolidation, exchange of shares or the like, (ii) a Requisite Shareholder acquires legal or beneficial ownership of any Company Shares after the date of this Agreement, or (iii) a Requisite Shareholder acquires the right to vote or share in the voting of any Company Shares after the date of this Agreement (collectively, the “ New Securities ”), the term “ Subject Shares ” shall be deemed to refer to and include such New Securities (including all such share dividends and distributions and any securities into which or for which any or all of the Subject Shares may be changed or exchanged into). 4.7 Shareholders’ Consent, Authorization or Approval . Each Requisite Shareholder hereby irrevocably agrees and confirms that, insofar as (i) such Requisite Shareholder’s consent, authorization or approval is required, or (ii) such Requisite Shareholder forms part of a class of shareholders of the Company whose consent, authorization or approval is required, in any such case in respect of or in connection with the Transactions, the Business Combination Agreement and the other transaction documents contemplated hereby and thereby, including pursuant to the Governing Documents of the Company, such Requisite Shareholder hereby grants, provides and gives such consent, authorization or approval, and all specific resolutions that may be required to have been adopted by such Requisite Shareholder or class of shareholders in connection with the Transactions, the Business Combination Agreement (as the Business Combination Agreement exists on the date hereof) and the other transaction documents contemplated hereby and thereby (as such transaction documents exists on the date hereof), are hereby deemed adopted and approved by such Requisite Shareholder (each as is in effect on the date hereof). For the avoidance of doubt, no Requisite Shareholder is providing its consent, authorization or approval under this Section 4.7 with respect to any future amendment, modification or supplement to the Business Combination Agreement or any other transaction document. 4.8 Irrevocable Proxy . Each Requisite Shareholder hereby unconditionally and irrevocably grants to, and appoints, the Company and any individual designated in writing by the Company, and each of them individually, as the Shareholder’s proxy and attorney-in-fact (with full power of substitution), for and in the name, place and stead of the Shareholder, to vote the Subject Shares, or grant a written consent or approval in respect of the Subject Shares, in a manner consistent with Section 3. The Requisite Shareholder agrees to execute such documents or certificates evidencing such proxy or power of attorney as the Company may reasonably request. The Requisite Shareholder understands and acknowledges that the Company is entering into the Business Combination Agreement in reliance upon the Shareholder’s execution and delivery of this Agreement. The Shareholder hereby affirms that the irrevocable proxy and power of attorney set forth in this Section 4.8 are given in connection with the execution of the Business Combination Agreement, and that such irrevocable proxy and power of attorney are given to secure a proprietary interest or the performance of obligations owed to the Company and may under no circumstances be revoked. The Requisite Shareholder hereby ratifies and confirms all that such irrevocable proxy and power of attorney may lawfully do or cause to be done by virtue hereof. SUCH IRREVOCABLE PROXY AND POWER OF ATTORNEY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 4.8 IS COUPLED WITH AN INTEREST AND IS IRREVOCABLE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROVISIONS OF THE POWERS OF ATTORNEY ACT (AS REVISED) OF THE CAYMAN ISLANDS. The irrevocable proxy and power of attorney granted hereunder shall be valid until the termination of this Agreement in accordance with its terms. Without limiting the foregoing, the irrevocable proxy and power of attorney granted hereunder shall not be revoked by the death, incapacity or bankruptcy of the Shareholder, or if the Shareholder is a body corporate, by its winding-up or dissolution. 5. Representations and Warranties of the Requisite Shareholders . Each Requisite Shareholder hereby, severally and not jointly, represents and warrants to Acquiror, the Company and Pubco as follows: 5.1 Ownership of the Company Shares . Such Requisite Shareholder is either (a) the owner of the Company Shares indicated on Schedule A hereto opposite such Requisite Shareholder’s name, free and clear of any and all Liens, other than (i) those created by this Agreement or (ii) as may be set forth in the Governing Documents of the Company or (b) has the power to vote (including, without limitation, by proxy or power of attorney) the Company Shares indicated on Schedule A hereto opposite such Requisite Shareholder’s name. Such Requisite Shareholder has as of the date hereof and, except pursuant to a Transfer permitted in accordance with Section 2.1 hereof, will have until the Expiration Time, sole voting power (including the right to control such vote as contemplated herein), power of disposition, power to issue instructions with respect to the matters set forth in this Agreement and power to agree to all of the matters applicable to such Requisite Shareholder set forth in this Agreement, in each case, over all Subject Shares. As of the date hereof, such Requisite Shareholder does not own any other voting securities of the Company or have the power to vote (including by proxy or power of attorney) any other voting securities of the Company other than the Company Shares set forth on Schedule A opposite such Requisite Shareholder’s name. As of the date hereof, such Requisite Shareholder does not own any rights to purchase or acquire (i) any other equity securities of the Company or (ii) the power to vote any other voting securities of the Company, in each case except as set forth on Schedule A opposite such Requisite Shareholder’s name. There are no claims for finder’s fees or brokerage commissions or other like payments in connection with this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby payable by such Requisite Shareholder pursuant to arrangements made by such Requisite Shareholder. 5.2 Absence of Other Voting Agreement . Except for this Agreement, such Requisite Shareholder has not: (a) entered into any voting agreement, voting trust or similar agreement with respect to any Subject Shares or other equity securities of the Company owned by such Requisite Shareholder or (b) granted any proxy, consent or power of attorney with respect to any Subject Shares or other equity securities of the Company owned by such Requisite Shareholder (other than as contemplated by this Agreement). 5.3 Due Authority . Such Requisite Shareholder has the full power and authority to make, enter into and carry out the terms of this Agreement. This Agreement has been duly and validly executed and delivered by such Requisite Shareholder (and, if such Requisite Shareholder is married and any of such Requisite Shareholder’s Subject Shares constitute community property or otherwise need spousal or other approval for this Agreement to be valid and binding, such Requisite Shareholder’s spouse), and constitutes a valid and binding agreement of such Requisite Shareholder enforceable against it in accordance with its terms (except as such enforceability may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, fraudulent transfer, reorganization, moratorium and other similar Laws of general applicability relating to or affecting creditor’s rights, and to general equitable principles). 5.4 No Conflict; Consents . (a) The execution and delivery of this Agreement by such Requisite Shareholder does not, and the performance by such Requisite Shareholder of the obligations under this Agreement and the compliance by such Requisite Shareholder with the provisions hereof do not and will not: (i) conflict with or violate any Law applicable to such Requisite Shareholder, (ii) contravene or conflict with, or result in any violation or breach of, any provision of any charter, certificate of incorporation, limited liability company agreement, certificate of formation, articles of association, by-laws, operating agreement or similar formation or governing documents and instruments of such Requisite Shareholder, as applicable, or (iii) result in any breach of or constitute a default (or an event that with notice or lapse of time or both would become a default) under, or give to others any rights of termination, amendment, acceleration or cancellation of, or result in the creation of a Lien on any of the Subject Shares owned by such Requisite Shareholder pursuant to any contract or agreement to which such Requisite Shareholder is a party or by which such Requisite Shareholder is bound, except in the case of clause (i) or (iii) as would not reasonably be expected, either individually or in the aggregate, to materially impair the ability of such Requisite Shareholder to perform its obligations hereunder or to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. (b) No consent, approval, order or authorization of, or registration, declaration or filing with, any Governmental Authority or any other person is required by or with respect to such Requisite Shareholder in connection with the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the consummation by such Requisite Shareholder of the transactions contemplated hereby. If such Requisite Shareholder is a natural person, no consent of such Requisite Shareholder’s spouse is necessary under any “community property” or other Laws in order for such Requisite Shareholder to enter into and perform its obligations under this Agreement. 5.5 Absence of Litigation . As of the date hereof, there is no Action pending or, to the knowledge of such Requisite Shareholder, threatened, against such Requisite Shareholder that would reasonably be expected to impair the ability of such Requisite Shareholder to perform such Requisite Shareholder’s obligations hereunder or to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. 5.6 Reliance by Acquiror, the Company and Pubco . Such Requisite Shareholder understands and acknowledges that each of Acquiror, the Company and Pubco is entering into the Business Combination Agreement in reliance upon such Requisite Shareholder’s execution and delivery of this Agreement. 5.7 Requisite Shareholder Has Adequate Information . Such Requisite Shareholder is a sophisticated shareholder and has adequate information concerning the business and financial condition of Acquiror and the Company to make an informed decision regarding this Agreement and the Transactions, and has independently, without reliance upon Acquiror or the Company, and based on such information as such Requisite Shareholder has deemed appropriate, made its own analysis and decision to enter into this Agreement. Such Requisite Shareholder acknowledges that none of Acquiror or the Company has made or makes any representation or warranty, whether express or implied, of any kind or character with respect to the matters covered herein, in each case except as expressly set forth in this Agreement. Such Requisite Shareholder acknowledges that the agreements contained herein with respect to the Subject Shares held by such Requisite Shareholder are irrevocable. 6. Termination . This Agreement shall terminate upon the Expiration Time. The termination of this Agreement shall not relieve any party from any liability arising in respect of any willful and material breach of this Agreement prior to such termination. 7. Miscellaneous . 7.1 Further Assurances . From time to time, at another Party’s request and without further consideration, each Party shall execute and deliver such additional documents and take all such further action as may be reasonably necessary or desirable to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. 7.2 Fees and Expenses. E ach of the Parties shall be responsible for its own fees and expenses (including, the fees and expenses of investment bankers, accountants and counsel) in connection with the entering into of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby; provided that the fees and expenses of Acquiror and the Company shall be allocated as set forth in Section 12.6 of the Business Combination Agreement. 7.3 No Ownership Interest . Nothing contained in this Agreement shall be deemed to vest in Acquiror, Pubco, the Merger Sub I or the Merger Sub II any direct or indirect ownership or incidence of ownership of or with respect to any Subject Shares. 7.4 Amendments, Waivers . This Agreement may not be amended except by an instrument in writing signed by each of the Parties hereto. At any time prior to the Expiration Time, (a) Acquiror may (i) extend the time for the performance of any obligation or other act of any Requisite Shareholder, (ii) waive any inaccuracy in the representations and warranties of each Requisite Shareholder contained herein or in any document delivered by any Requisite Shareholder pursuant hereto and (iii) waive compliance with any agreement of each Requisite Shareholder or any condition to their obligations contained herein and any such extension or waiver shall be valid if set forth in an instrument in writing signed by Acquiror; (b) the Requisite Shareholders may (i) extend the time for the performance of any obligation or other act of Acquiror or the Company, (ii) waive any inaccuracy in the representations and warranties of Acquiror or the Company contained herein or in any document delivered by Acquiror or the Company pursuant hereto and (iii) waive compliance with any agreement of Acquiror or the Company or any condition to their obligations contained herein. 7.5 Notices . All notices, requests, claims, demands and other communications hereunder shall be in writing and shall be given (and shall be deemed to have been duly given upon receipt) by delivery in person, by email or by registered or certified mail (postage prepaid, return receipt requested) to the respective Parties at the following addresses (or at such other address for a Party as shall be specified in a notice given in accordance with this Section 7.5 ): if to Acquiror: Starlink AI Acquisition Corporation 605 W 42nd Street, New York, NY 10036 Attention: Gus Liu, Chief Executive Officer Email: hengsenburgliu@gmail.com with copies (which shall not constitute notice) to: Ekberg, Fagre & Seem LLP Attn: Alan Seem Email: aseem@efs-law.com if to the Company or Pubco: Spider Digital Technology Ltd. One Raffles Place #50-00 Singapore 048616 Attn: Chen Hua Email: jackchen2086@gmail.com with copies (which shall not constitute notice) to: DLA Piper LLP 20th Floor, South Tower, Beijing Kerry Center 1 Guanghua Road Chaoyang District Beijing 100020 China Attn: Yang Ge James Chang Telephone No.: +86 10 8520 0616 +86 10 8520 0608 Email: yang.ge@dlapiper.com james.chang@dlapiper.com if to any Requisite Shareholder, to the address for notice set forth on Schedule A hereto, 7.6 Headings . The descriptive headings contained in this Agreement are included for convenience of reference only and shall not affect in any way the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. 7.7 Severability . If any term or other provision of this Agreement is invalid, illegal or incapable of being enforced by any rule of law, or public policy, all other conditions and provisions of this Agreement shall nevertheless remain in full force and effect so long as the economic or legal substance of the transactions contemplated hereby or any of the other Transactions is not affected in any manner materially adverse to any Party. Upon such determination that any term or other provision is invalid, illegal or incapable of being enforced, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to modify this Agreement so as to effect the original intent of the Parties as closely as possible in a mutually acceptable manner in order that the transactions contemplated by this Agreement be consummated as originally contemplated to the fullest extent possible. 7.8 Entire Agreement; Assignment . This Agreement and the schedules hereto (together with each transaction document in connection with the Transactions to which the Parties hereto are parties, to the extent referred to herein) constitute the entire agreement among the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersede all prior agreements and undertakings, both written and oral, among the Parties, or any of them, with respect to the subject matter hereof. Except for transfers permitted by Section 2.1 , this Agreement shall not be assigned (whether pursuant to a merger, by operation of law or otherwise) by any Party without the prior express written consent of the other Parties hereto. 7.9 Certificates . Promptly following the date of this Agreement, the Company shall advise its transfer agent in writing that each Requisite Shareholder’s Subject Shares are subject to the restrictions set forth herein and, in connection therewith, provide the transfer agent of the Company, as applicable, in writing with such information as is reasonable to ensure compliance with such restrictions. 7.10 Parties in Interest . This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure solely to the benefit of each Party, and nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other person any right, benefit or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement. 7.11 Interpretation . (a) Unless the context of this Agreement otherwise requires, (i) words of any gender include each other gender, (ii) words using the singular or plural number also include the plural or singular number, respectively, (iii) the definitions contained in this agreement are applicable to the other grammatical forms of such terms, (iv) the terms “hereof,” “herein,” “hereby,” “hereto” and derivative or similar words refer to this entire Agreement, (v) the terms “Section” and “Schedule” refer to the specified Section or Schedule of or to this Agreement, (vi) the word “including” means “including without limitation,” (vii) the word “or” shall be disjunctive but not exclusive, (viii) the word “person” means an individual, corporation, partnership, limited partnership, limited liability company, syndicate, person (including, without limitation, a “person” as defined in Section 13(d)(3) of the Exchange Act), trust, association or entity or government, political subdivision, agency or instrumentality of a government, and references to a person are also to its permitted successors and assigns, (ix), an “affiliate” of a specified person means a person who, directly or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with, such specified person, (x) references to agreements and other documents shall be deemed to include all subsequent amendments and other modifications thereto and references to any Law shall include all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder and (xi) references to any Law shall be construed as including all statutory, legal, and regulatory provisions consolidating, amending or replacing such Law. (b) The language used in this Agreement shall be deemed to be the language chosen by the Parties to express their mutual intent and no rule of strict construction shall be applied against any Party. 7.12 Governing Law . This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the Laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts executed in and to be performed in that State. All legal actions and proceedings arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be heard and determined exclusively in any federal and state courts located in the City of New York, Borough of Manhattan (the “ Specified Courts ”). The Parties hereby (a) irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the aforesaid Specified Courts for themselves and with respect to their respective properties for the purpose of any Action arising out of or relating to this Agreement brought by any Party, and (b) agree not to commence any Action relating thereto except in the Specified Courts, other than Actions in any court of competent jurisdiction to enforce any judgment, decree or award rendered by any such Specified Courts. Each of the Parties further agrees that notice as provided herein shall constitute sufficient service of process and the Parties further waive any argument that such service is insufficient. Each of the Parties hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives, and agrees not to assert, by way of motion or as a defense, counterclaim or otherwise, in any Action arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby any claim (a) that it is not personally subject to the jurisdiction of the Specified Courts for any reason, (b) that it or its property is exempt or immune from jurisdiction of any such Specified Court or from any legal process commenced in such Specified Courts (whether through service of notice, attachment prior to judgment, attachment in aid of execution of judgment, execution of judgment or otherwise) and (c) that (i) the Action in any such Specified Court is brought in an inconvenient forum, (ii) the venue of such Action is improper or (iii) this Agreement, or the subject matter hereof, may not be enforced in or by such Specified Courts. 7.13 Specific Performance . The Parties agree that irreparable damage would occur if any provision of this Agreement were not performed in accordance with the terms hereof, and, accordingly, that the Parties shall be entitled to an injunction or injunctions to prevent breaches of this Agreement or to enforce specifically the performance of the terms and provisions hereof in the Specified Courts without proof of actual damages or otherwise, in addition to any other remedy to which they are entitled at law or in equity as expressly permitted in this Agreement. Each of the Parties hereby further waives (a) any defense in any action for specific performance that a remedy at law would be adequate and (b) any requirement under any Law to post security or a bond as a prerequisite to obtaining equitable relief. 7.14 WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL . EACH OF THE PARTIES HEREBY WAIVES TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY WITH RESPECT TO ANY LITIGATION DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY ARISING OUT OF, UNDER OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY. EACH OF THE PARTIES (A) CERTIFIES THAT NO REPRESENTATIVE, AGENT OR ATTORNEY OF ANY OTHER PARTY HAS REPRESENTED, EXPRESSLY OR OTHERWISE, THAT SUCH OTHER PARTY WOULD NOT, IN THE EVENT OF LITIGATION, SEEK TO ENFORCE THE FOREGOING WAIVER AND (B) ACKNOWLEDGES THAT IT AND THE OTHER PARTIES HERETO HAVE BEEN INDUCED TO ENTER INTO THIS AGREEMENT AND THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY, AS APPLICABLE, BY, AMONG OTHER THINGS, THE MUTUAL WAIVERS AND CERTIFICATIONS IN THIS SECTION 7.14 . 7.15 Counterparts; Electronic Delivery . This Agreement may be executed and delivered (including by facsimile or portable document format (.pdf) transmission) in one or more counterparts, and by the different Parties hereto in separate counterparts, each of which when executed shall be deemed to be an original but all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same agreement. Delivery by email to counsel for the other Parties of a counterpart executed by a Party shall be deemed to meet the requirements of the previous sentence. 7.16 Directors and Officers . Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to impose any obligation or limitation on votes or actions taken by any director, officer, employee, agent, designee or other representative of any Requisite Shareholder or by any Requisite Shareholder that is a natural person, in each case, in his or her capacity as a director or officer of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries. Each Requisite Shareholder is executing this Agreement solely in such capacity as a record or beneficial holder of Company Shares.
